item.title: A lower bound for additive complements to the primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the size of sets $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains every sufficiently large integer. We obtain $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This gives a quantitative form of Conjecture 2 of Ruzsa and excludes additive complements of size $O(\log X)$, as asked in one part of Erd\H{o}s Problem 32. More generally, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ in $[X/2,X]$, whenever this number is positive.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Radomskii

item.title: On the calculation of an integral introduced by Hubert Delange
item.description: arXiv:2610.14249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In his paper, ''Sur la distribution des fractions irr\'eductibles de d\'enominateur $n$ ou de d\'enominateur au plus \'egal \`a $x$'', Hubert Delange considers the family integrals defined by \begin{equation*} \int_0^1\left(\frac{N(n,t)}{\phi(n)}-t\right)^{2q}dt, \end{equation*} where $n>1$ and $q>0$ are positive integers, $\phi$ is the Euler totient function, and for any real number $t>0$, $N(n,t)$ counts the number reduced fractions whith denominator $n$ that belong to the interval $]0,t]$. He was able to evaluate the integral for $q=1$ but stated that ''Malheureusement, nous n'avons pas su jusqu'\`a pr\'esent faire cette \'evaluation pour $q>1$''. In addition to its intrinsic interest, this calculation would help understand the asymptotic distribution of the $\phi(n)$ totatives of $n$ relative to $\phi(n)$ equidistributed numbers in $[0,n]$. In this paper, we first provide some general properties of the integral for any $q>1$ and reduce the problem to its calculation for odd square-free integers with at least two distinct prime factors. We then analyse into more detail the case $q=2$ for which we provide a formula that reduces the problem to the evaluation of the fourfold M\"obius sum, of integer valued modular sums related to generalized Dedekind sums.
item.dc:creator: Steven Brown

item.title: Bounds for the residue of Dedekind zeta functions under GRH and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.14257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\kappa_{\mathbb{K}}$ be the residue at $1$ of the Dedekind zeta function of a number field $\mathbb{K}$. We prove explicit upper and lower bounds for $\kappa_{\mathbb{K}}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH). Previous explicit bounds of comparable generality are weaker and require a weak form of Artin's holomorphy conjecture: our bounds improve the constants while assuming only GRH for the relevant Dedekind zeta functions. The new lower bound enables all imaginary quadratic fields with class number $\leq 2000$ to be detected (assuming GRH). Furthermore, we demonstrate that the upper bound can be significantly reduced when considering extensions of any fixed, nontrivial field.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Ramon Garcia, Lo\"ic Greni\'e, Ethan Simpson Lee, Giuseppe Molteni

item.title: On the generalization of Christol's theorem to domains of finite type over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.14450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize Christol's theorem---which characterizes algebraic power series over a finite field in terms of automatic coefficient sequences---to completions of domains of finite type over a finite field~$\mathbb{F}_{q}$. Let $A$ be such a domain of dimension~$d$ and $\mathfrak{a}$ an ideal of depth~$d$. In the $\mathfrak{a}$-adic completion $\hat{A}$, choose an $\hat{A}$-regular sequence $\boldsymbol{x}=\{x_{1},\dots,x_{d}\}\subset\hat{\mathfrak{a}}$ and a set of representatives $E$ of $\hat{A}/(\boldsymbol{x})$ that is an $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-vector subspace consisting of algebraic elements. Every element $y\in\hat{A}$ then admits a unique expansion $y=\sum_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}a_{u}x^{u}$ with coefficients $a_{u}\in E$. We prove that $y$ is algebraic over $A$ if and only if the coefficient sequence $\{a_{u}\}_{u\in\mathbb{N}^{d}}$ is $q$-automatic. The proof relies on a careful study of henselizations, which are shown to coincide with the algebraic closures inside the completions under certain conditions. As an application, we obtain a complete characterization of the automaticity of $\beta$-expansions for formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$, answering questions posed by Hbaib--Mkaouar and Scheicher--Sirvent.
item.dc:creator: Lian Duan, Chunlin Wang

item.title: The strong Ramanujan bound for Drinfeld modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.14458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Ramanujan bound states that the degree of the trace of the $\mathfrak{p}$-Hecke operator on a space of weight $k$ Drinfeld cusp forms is at most $d(k-2)/2$, where $\mathfrak{p}$ is a prime of degree $d$ in $\mathbb{F}_q[T]$. We prove the strong Ramanujan bound, which states that at level 1, this bound can be improved to $d(k-(q+1))/2$. In addition, we classify when the strong Ramanujan bound is sharp; surprisingly, this turns out to depend on $\mathfrak{p}$ only through the parity of its degree. We also prove results related to the smallest slope of the Atkin operator and mod $p$ distributions of Frobenius polynomials of Drinfeld modules over finite fields.
item.dc:creator: Sjoerd de Vries

item.title: Sharp Constants and Extremizers in Homogeneous Tree BMO
item.description: arXiv:2610.14459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a finite-tree formalism for sharp inequalities on real-valued, mean-centered $\operatorname{L}^1$-BMO over homogeneous $q$-ary filtrations. A reduction theorem identifies local and global sharp constants with the supremum of finite-depth constants. Finite anchoring gives compact optimization problems and rational extremizers under rational piecewise-linear hypotheses, while stable centering shows that imposing zero root average preserves the supremum over all depths. The principal application is the absolute-value map: we construct centered examples in which taking absolute values increases the BMO seminorm and obtain bounds strictly below the universal factor $2$. Jensen-defect Carleson functionals and martingale-difference envelopes provide further applications, illustrating distinct anchoring mechanisms and the differences between finite-depth rationality, stabilization, and global attainment.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Mohajer

item.title: Simultaneous Unimodularity of Positive Integer Matrices and Their Entrywise Cubes
item.description: arXiv:2610.14546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We solve an open problem posed by Richard Guy in his book Unsolved Problems in Number Theory. We prove that, for every integer $n\geq10$, there exist infinitely many $n\times n$ integer matrices $A$ such that every entry is $\ge2$ and $\det A=\det A^{[3]}=1$, where $A^{[3]}$ denotes the entrywise cube of $A$. The matrices may be chosen compatibly, so they can form the leading principal blocks of a single infinite positive integer array. The order-ten case is reduced to an inhomogeneous system consisting of one linear and one diagonal cubic equation. The circle method then provides infinitely many positive integral solutions. To pass from order $n$ to order $n+1$, we introduce a bordering construction that preserves the signed cofactor vectors of both the matrix and its entrywise cube. Iterating this construction yields the result in every order $n\geq10$.
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Li, Shuochen Wang, Zimeng Ye, Alexandru Zaharescu

item.title: On trace-zero norm forms of orders of rational quaternion algebras with applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.14613v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, by normalizing the trace-zero norm forms according to the parity of orders of definite rational quaternion algebras, we give an explicit formulation to the even Clifford correspondence followed by the reciprocity of ternary forms. We obtain an exact identity between ternary representation numbers and the number of elements of an order with prescribed reduced norm and trace, which applies to all orders without squarefreeness constraint on the reduced discriminant. Applications include a criterion for realizing ternary forms as trace-zero norm forms, a formula for traces of Brandt matrices in terms of representation numbers, and explicit theta series relations associated with local reciprocity. We also describe reciprocal orders and order chains, and interpret the ternary forms occurring in the congruent number problem through their associated quaternion orders.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Luo, Tianze Wang, Haigang Zhou

item.title: Examples of Bessel Functions of Order Zero Related to the Functional Equation of the Riemann Zeta Function
item.description: arXiv:2610.14628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 2010, M. A. Chaudhry et al. introduced a class of functions Sigma satisfying an L^1-condition. They proved that every function phi in Sigma gives rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. They also provided an example of a function outside Sigma for which the functional equation still holds. In this paper, we present several examples of Bessel functions of order zero that do not belong to Sigma but nevertheless give rise to the functional equation for the Riemann zeta function. In particular, we show that J_0(a sqrt(x)), J_0(ax), and Y_0(x) exhibit this phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Hideto Iwata

item.title: Bounds for (k,c) model functions over p-adic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.14744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a $p$-adic field, let $k,c\ge1$, and let $\rho$ be a $(k,c)$ representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{kc}(F)$: a complex representation of finite length whose wave front set has $(k^c)$ as its unique maximal orbit, and which admits a $(k,c)$ functional that is unique up to scaling. We prove that the functions in the $(k,c)$ model of $\rho$ are of moderate growth, by relating this model to the Zelevinsky model of $\rho$, and obtain as a consequence a bound for the restriction of these functions to the standard Levi subgroup associated with the composition $(c^k)$ of $kc$. As applications, we study convergence problems of several integrals involving $(k,c)$ models: integrals from the generalized doubling method, and a new family of integrals which extends the Rankin--Selberg integrals for Speh representations of Lapid and Mao.
item.dc:creator: Eyal Kaplan

item.title: Exact Rank of the Largest Good Lattice Point Matrix
item.description: arXiv:2610.15042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that for every integer $n>2$ the largest good lattice point matrix $U_n=[u_h:h\in H_n]$, whose columns are generated by all integers $h<n$ coprime to $n$, has rank exactly $\varphi(n)/2+1$. The upper bound follows from the pairing identity $u_h+u_{n-h}=(n,\dots,n,2n)^{\top}$. For the lower bound the columns are centered and the resulting orbit under the multiplicative group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^{\times}$ is analysed by means of odd Dirichlet characters; the essential arithmetic input is the non-vanishing of $\sum_{a}a\,\psi(a)$ for odd primitive characters $\psi$, which is equivalent to Dirichlet's theorem $L(1,\psi)\neq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Long-Hao Xu

item.title: Proof of Two Conjectural $q$-Supercongruences Related to Van Hamme's $\mathrm{(G.2)}$ Supercongruence
item.description: arXiv:2610.15050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove two conjectures concerning parametric $q$- supercongruences related to Van Hamme's $\mathrm{(G.2)}$ supercongruence. First, we confirm Tang\rq s conjecture \cite[Conjecture $4.1$]{Tang G2} by establishing the corresponding congruences modulo $[m]\Phi_m(q)^2$. Second, we prove a conjecture of Wang and Xu \cite[Conjecture $2$]{WangXu24}, extending their $q$-supercongruence modulo $\Phi_m(q)^5$ to modulo $[m]\Phi_m(q)^4$ when $m\equiv1\pmod4$.
item.dc:creator: Liton Karmakar, Arijit Jana

item.title: Kitaoka's conjecture for real cyclotomic fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15109v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Kitaoka's conjecture for all real cyclotomic fields, i.e. for fields of the form $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_k+\zeta_k^{-1})$ where $\zeta_k$ is a primitive $k$th root of unity. More precisely, we show that such a field admits a universal classical ternary quadratic form if and only if it is a real quadratic field.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Kr\'asensk\'y

item.title: On a variant of the Piatetski-Shapiro prime number theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.15140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Denote by $\Pi_\gamma(x)$ the number of primes $p \leqslant x$ such that $[p^{1/\gamma}]$ is also a prime. In this paper, it is proved that the expected asymptotic formula \begin{equation*} \Pi_\gamma(x)=\frac{\gamma x}{(\log x)^2} (1+o(1)) \end{equation*} holds for $\gamma > 15/13$, which constitutes an improvement upon the previous result of Balog [2] who showed that the above asymptotic formula holds for $\gamma > 6/5$.
item.dc:creator: Linji Long, Jinjiang Li, Min Zhang

item.title: On Waring-Goldbach problem for two squares, three biquadratics, one quintic and one septic
item.description: arXiv:2610.15142v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, it is proved that every sufficiently large odd integer $n$ can be represented as \begin{equation*} n=p_1^2+p_2^2+p_3^4+p_4^4+p_5^4+p_6^5+p_7^7, \end{equation*} where $p_1,\dots,p_7$ are prime variables. This result constitutes an enhancement upon a previous result of Andrade [1].
item.dc:creator: Linji Long, Jinjiang Li, Min Zhang

item.title: A quotient of the Bruhat-Tits building classifying maximal matrix orders over curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.15147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a previous work, we defined a quotient graph of the Bruhat-Tits tree associated to the degree two special linear group over a local field whose vertex set is in correspondence with the maximal orders in a certain number of spinor genera. This graph has been applied to the study of the structure of some arithmetic groups, their presentations and their (co)homology groups. The genera of Eichler orders, which, for instance, are related to the problem of finding a basis that simultaneously splits two vector bundles with the same generic fiber, can often be described in terms of simpler genera via quotients. Furthermore, some embedding problems of orders can be studied via quotient graphs. These results provide a geometric framework for the study of maximal orders over function fields. In this article, we extend that construction to a higher dimensional setting through the use of singular chain complexes. Then we describe the set of vertices in this quotient that correspond to split maximal orders and the topology of the corresponding region of the quotient complex. More precisely, we show that these ``split vertices'' fall into a finite number of quotients of apartments by suitable subgroups of the corresponding Weyl group, the symmetric group. We relate these ``quotient apartments'' with the cuspidal sectors defined by previous authors who studied the quotient by the group of integral points of the special linear group. Both quotients are indeed related by a ramified cover that is unramified on cusps, as proved here.
item.dc:creator: Luis Arenas-Carmona, Claudio Bravo, Ignacio Saavedra

item.title: Deformation and Symmetry in Two Hypergeometric Supercongruences
item.description: arXiv:2610.15176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two supercongruence conjectures of Li--Long--Tu concerning truncated very-well-poised ${}_7F_6(1)$ series and Fourier coefficients of modular forms. The proofs are based on a common deformation method. By deforming the original truncated hypergeometric series to suitable terminating series, we are able to apply classical hypergeometric transformations together with Mishev's $W(D_5)$ symmetry. This reduces both problems to congruences for lower-rank hypergeometric sums that can be treated using the $p$-adic methods of Long--Tu--Yui--Zudilin. Although the two cases require different local arithmetic calculations, their global proof structure is the same. The resulting argument gives a unified explanation of these two supercongruences and suggests that the same deformation-and-symmetry method may apply more broadly.
item.dc:creator: Dianbin Bao

item.title: Post-critically finite polynomials over cyclotomic closures of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15257v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that, for any number field K and and d at least 2, there are at most finitely many monic, centred, post-critically finite polynomials of degree d with coefficients in the extension of K by all roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Ingram, Jorge Mello

item.title: Bernoulli numbers and the integer group determinants of $C_p \times C_p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a prime $p\ge7$, let $S(C_p\times C_p)$ be the set of integer group determinants and $e(p)$ the least exponent for which $p^{e(p)}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Let $r_p$ be the least integer $r\ge1$ satisfying $(2r+1)i>r(p-1)$ for every irregular pair $(p,2i)$ with $r\mid i$. We prove the unconditional inclusion $p^{p+3+2r_p}\mathbf Z\subseteq S(C_p\times C_p)$. Equality $e(p)=p+3+2r_p$ holds when Vandiver's conjecture holds for $p$ and $r_p\le(p-5)/2$, hence for every prime $7\le p<2^{31}$. The first exception to $e(p)=p+5$ is $p=103$, where $e(103)=116$. A polynomial obstruction from Bernoulli numbers supplies the lower bound, and circular units give the construction. For regular primes, we characterize the entire determinant set through explicit affine systems over $\mathbf F_p$ and principality conditions in $\mathbf Z[\zeta_p]$. For regular $p\ge11$, prime cofactors cannot occur at valuation $p+3$; at valuation $p+4$ they have natural density $(p+1)/(hp^{(p-3)/2})$, where $h$ is the class number of $\mathbf Q(\zeta_p)$. We also show that $p^{p+5}$ is the least absolute value of a nonzero $p$-divisible determinant for these regular primes.
item.dc:creator: Chatchawan Panraksa

item.title: The Norm Spectrum of Barnes-Wall Lattices Below Twice the Minimum
item.description: arXiv:2610.15288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda_m$ be the Barnes-Wall lattice of dimension $2^m$, normalized to have minimum squared norm $d_m:=2^{m-1}$. We determine its complete norm spectrum strictly between $d_m$ and $2d_m$, proving that, for every integer $m\ge1$, $\{\|x\|^2:x\in\Lambda_m,\ d_m<\|x\|^2<2d_m\}=\{2d_m-2^j:j\in\mathbb Z,\ \lceil m/2\rceil\le j\le m-2\}$. In particular, the norm spectrum in this interval is nonempty for $m\ge4$. The proof uses a Gaussian-integer model in which lattice automorphisms arising from Clifford unitaries transform a vector into a pair of coordinate subvectors in a lower-dimensional lattice. Divisibility of the differences of their squared norms and a matrix Parseval identity provide the arithmetic and averaging constraints needed for induction on $m$. Every listed norm is realized explicitly by a sum of two minimal vectors of the lattice.
item.dc:creator: Yuhang Cao, Sihuang Hu, Hexiang Huang, Mengrui Yang

item.title: Refining the 7/8 zero-free half-plane for Hecke and Dirichlet L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, OpenAI announced a uniform $7/8$ zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{-3})$, together with its transfer to Dirichlet $L$-functions. Assuming the analytic inputs of that work, we improve the boundary from $7/8=0.875$ to $8748867/10000000=0.8748867$ for the same families. The improvement combines a relaxed direct estimate with an amplified first moment of the reflected numerator, obtained from the existing fourth-moment estimate. A two-stage parameter argument yields the stated boundary without strengthening the inverse-moment estimate.
item.dc:creator: Hejian Sang

item.title: Counting Rational Points on a Certain Bihomogeneous Threefold
item.description: arXiv:2610.15315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $V\subset\mathbb P^2\times\mathbb P^2$ be the threefold $x_0y_0^2+x_1y_1^2+x_2y_2^2=0$, and let $U$ be the complement of its coordinate hyperplane sections. For the anticanonical height $H([\mathbf x],[\mathbf y])=|\mathbf x|^2|\mathbf y|$, evaluated on primitive integral representatives, we prove \[ N_U(B)=\frac{12\pi-14}{\zeta(2)\zeta(3)}B\log B+o(B\log B). \] The two projections combine lattice counting with uniform conic estimates. The main arithmetic step is an average of the fiber singular series, whose two main terms are related by Hilbert reciprocity. A moment estimate controls the full bad-prime part, and shape estimates permit the errors to be summed over the height region. We also check the leading constant with Peyre's constant.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Zhao

item.title: Non-vanishing of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic L-functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15316v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish lower bounds for the non-vanishing proportions of primitive cubic, quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $\F_q[T]$ in the non-Kummer setting. Adapting the truncated-exponential method of Gao and Zhao, we improve the cubic lower bound of David, Florea and Lal\'in and obtain positive lower bounds for quartic and sextic families in which every ramified local character has full order. For each family, the lower limit of the non-vanishing proportion exceeds $e^{-e^{66}}$ as the conductor degree tends to infinity with $q$ fixed. We also establish uniform twisted first moments in the quartic and sextic cases, yielding an asymptotic formula for the sextic first moment. All results are unconditional.
item.dc:creator: Ziwei Hong

item.title: Monotonicity of Coefficients of Interpolated Multiple Zeta Values
item.description: arXiv:2610.15376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\zeta^t(\boldsymbol{k})=\sum_{d=1}^{r}S_d(\boldsymbol{k})t^{r-d}$ be the interpolated multiple zeta value of an admissible index $\boldsymbol{k}$ of depth $r$. We show the monotonicity property of coefficients $S_1(\boldsymbol{k})\ge\cdots\ge S_r(\boldsymbol{k})>0$. In the proof, we represent the coefficients as integrals over a common measure space and compares the integrands pointwise. As consequences, we determine the sign and vanishing of $\zeta^{-1}(\boldsymbol{k})$ and locate the zeros of $\zeta^t(\boldsymbol{k})$ in the closed unit disk.
item.dc:creator: Shuji Yamamoto

item.title: On strongly minimal asymptotic bases of order $h$ generated by powers of $2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $h\geq2$ be an integer and let $\mathbb{N}_0=W_1\cup\cdots\cup W_h$ be a partition into infinite sets. For $W\subseteq\mathbb{N}_0$, let $A(W)$ denote the set of all finite nonempty sums of distinct powers $2^w$ with $w\in W$. We give a necessary and sufficient condition for $A=A(W_1)\cup\cdots\cup A(W_h)$ to be a strongly minimal asymptotic basis of order $h$. This provides a complete answer to a problem posed by Nathanson in 1988.
item.dc:creator: Shi-Qiang Chen, Xin-Yue Yan

item.title: On the OpenAI proof that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist
item.description: arXiv:2610.15483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A recent manuscript of OpenAI asserts that Landau-Siegel zeros do not exist. Here, we give a detailed account of its argument, arranged as a direct proof with explicit constants. There are absolute constants $q_0$ and $\delta_0>0$ such that, for every primitive real Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge q_0$, every real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q\ge\delta_0$, and one can take $q_0=10^{10}$ and $\delta_0=3.0\times 10^{-3}$. Combined with a recent computation of Lu, Zaman, and Zhao, this result yields the bound $(1-\beta)\log q\ge 3.0\times 10^{-3}$ for every conductor $q\ge 3$. The proof is an interpolation determinant argument in the biquadratic field generated by $\sqrt{2}$ over the quadratic field attached to $\chi$. A real zero close to one forces $\chi(p)=-1$ for most primes $p$, and the Frobenius congruence at these primes makes a certain nonzero determinant divisible by higher powers of these primes than its Archimedean size allows. The underlying ideas are those of the OpenAI manuscript. The explicit constants, and the presentation, are new.
item.dc:creator: William D. Banks

item.title: A linear independence criterion for $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta values at odd integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.15525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, a new criterion is established to obtain the linear independence of some values of the $p$-adic Hurwitz zeta function at odd integers $s\geq 3$. We generalize a theorem of F.~Beukers, who gave, among others, an alternative proof---using Pad\'{e} approximation theory---of a result originally due to F.~Calegari on the irrationality of the $p$-adic Riemann zeta value $\zeta_p(3)$ for $p = 2, 3$. To prove our main theorem, we work in a general setting, where we construct and study new Pad\'e approximants of Laurent series satisfying the functional equation $f(z) = f(1-z)$. This complements our previous work on the linear independence of $p$-adic polygamma values.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Kawashima, Anthony Po\"{e}ls

item.title: The Goldbach exceptional set: an exponent 7/12 and conditional refinement
item.description: arXiv:2610.15559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(E(X)\) count the even integers between \(4\) and \(X\) that are not sums of two primes. We combine Pintz's explicit formula for the major arcs with the exponential-sum estimate of Maynard, Pandey, and Radziwi{\l}{\l} to prove \(E(X)\ll_\varepsilon X^{7/12+\varepsilon}\) whenever all Dirichlet \(L\)-functions have a common fixed zero-free half-plane \(\Rea s>\theta_0\), with \(\theta_0<1\). The uniform \(7/8\) theorem reported in the OpenAI mathematics release supplies this input. Under the stronger hypothesis that every nontrivial Dirichlet zero has real part at most \(\theta\), where \(1/2\leq\theta\leq2/3\), we prove \[ E(X)\ll_{\theta,\varepsilon}X^{g(\theta)+\varepsilon}, \qquad g(\theta)=\frac{\theta(5-4\theta)}{2(2-\theta)}. \] Thus every fixed \(\theta<2/3\) gives an exponent strictly below \(7/12\). The latter argument uses a classical fixed-modulus zero-density estimate and is independent of the new exponential-sum theorem.
item.dc:creator: J\'anos Pintz, Ingo Alth\"ofer

item.title: Bloch torsion and modular combinations of Nahm sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.15587v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a positive-definite symmetric integral $12\times12$ matrix $A$ such that, for every solution $Q$ of Nahm's equations $1-Q=Q^A$ with $Q_i\ne0,1$ for all $i$, the associated element $\sum_i[Q_i]$ is torsion in the Bloch group of $\mathbb{Q}(Q_1,\ldots,Q_{12})$. However, the Nahm sum $F_{A,B,C}(\tau)$ is nonmodular for every $B\in\mathbb{Q}^{12}$ and $C\in\mathbb{Q}$. Thus the torsion condition for all solutions in Nahm's conjecture is not sufficient for the existence of a modular Nahm sum.
item.dc:creator: Xuejun Guo

item.title: Coprime pairs with equal sum of divisors, assuming smooth shifted primes
item.description: arXiv:2610.15674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $h(x)$ be the number of pairs $1\le a<b<x$ with $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $\sigma(a)=\sigma(b)$. Erd\H{o}s Problem #824 asks whether $h(x)>x^{2-o(1)}$. By an argument of Pollack and Pomerance, this follows if for every fixed $\delta>0$ there are $y^{1-o(1)}$ primes $p\le5y$ with $p+1$ free of prime factors exceeding $y^\delta$. We write this implication out with explicit parameters and formalize it in Lean 4. We then check that the argument of the recent OpenAI preprint "Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers", which claims the corresponding statement for $p-1$, applies to $p+1$ after a change of sign in two of its sections. Consequently $h(x)=x^{2-o(1)}$, conditionally on the correctness of that preprint, which has not been refereed and whose main new estimates we have not independently verified.
item.dc:creator: Shisheng Li, Zhong Zhuang

item.title: Counting subspaces with prescribed Welch sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.15694v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $q=2^n$ with $n=2m+1$ for an integer $m\ge1$, and let ${\mathbb F}_q$ be the finite field with $q$ elements. Let $W_n(x)=x^{2^m+3}$ be the Welch function on ${\mathbb F}_q$. For $1\le k\le n$ and $b\in{\mathbb F}_q$, denote by $N_{n,k}(b)$ the number of $k$-dimensional ${\mathbb F}_2$-subspaces $E$ of $\mathbb F}_q$ such that \[ \sum_{x\in E}W_n(x)=b. \] In this paper, we determine $N_{n,k}(b)$ for all $k$. The only nontrivial case is $k=3$, for which the answer is given in terms of a binary Kloosterman sum. As a consequence, we prove a recent conjecture of Hou and Zhao on the third-order sum-freedom of the Welch function.
item.dc:creator: Kaimin Cheng, Jie Hu

item.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation for Bernoulli Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.15700v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(\alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}\), and let \((\xi_n)_{n \ge 1}\) be independent random variables taking the values \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) with equal probability. We study the random walk \[X_n = \xi_1 + \cdots + \xi_n \pmod 1\] and present a deterministic Diophantine condition on \((\alpha, \beta)\) that implies almost sure Poisson pair correlation. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first result providing explicit examples in this framework where the increment measure is purely discrete. The classical Fourier contraction method fails in this setting; a different approach is required. Our proof uses the parabolic geometry of returns to \(1\) and an exact covariance formula for overlapping blocks.
item.dc:creator: Bo Tan, Zhen Zhang, Qing-Long Zhou

item.title: Solutions of $x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D$ with small $x_3$: a spectral approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.15706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We count the integral solutions of x_1^2+x_2^2-x_3^2=D weighted by Phi(x_3/M), for M smaller than sqrt(D). Such solutions correspond to binary quadratic forms of discriminant D, and the count becomes a sum, over the geodesics of discriminant D, of a function of their distance to the point i, which we evaluate by the spectral theory of automorphic forms. For square D=n^2 the geodesics run from cusp to cusp, and Hecke theory reduces them to a single geodesic. For every n and both parities of x_3 we obtain an asymptotic formula with error O(n^{1+theta+eps} M^{-1/2}), theta=7/64, using the Kim-Sarnak bound and the large sieve of Deshouillers and Iwaniec; it is non-trivial for M >= n^{71/96+eps}. This improves the range n^{5/6+eps} of the elementary method and confirms the corrected main term of the author's earlier work. For non-square D=f^2 D_0 the geodesics are closed, and a Hecke relation for their traces reduces everything to the fundamental discriminant D_0. For odd D_0 we obtain an error O(D^eps f^{1+theta} D_0^{2/3} M^{-1/2}), using the formulas of Duke-Imamoglu-Toth and Baruch-Mao together with Young's cubic moment. For D = 5 mod 8 this counts all solutions, and the range M >= D^{1/2-1/1332} of Friedlander and Iwaniec improves to M >= D^{4/9+eps}. This paper was written in collaboration with Claude (Opus 5.5, High), an AI model developed by Anthropic.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Baier

item.title: On the inverse Goldbach problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.15758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish two quantitative results concerning additive decompositions of the set $\mathbb{P}$ of primes. First, we prove that, if $A,B\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements and $A+B$ differs from the primes by only finitely many elements, then $$ \frac{\sqrt{x}}{\log x}\ll A(x),B(x) \ll \sqrt{x}. $$ Second, we show that, if $A,B,C\subseteq\mathbb N$ have at least two elements each, then $$ ((A+B+C)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\mathbb P)(x) \gg \frac{\sqrt{x}}{(\log x)^2}. $$ An analogous estimate is obtained for sumsets of $k\ge 3$ sets. The proofs use Montgomery's large sieve, Gallagher's larger sieve, a mean-value argument for a certain multiplicative function, and a submultiplicative sumset inequality.
item.dc:creator: Paolo Leonetti

item.title: Tribonacci numbers that are palindromic concatenations of two distinct repdigits
item.description: arXiv:2610.15770v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(T_n)_{n\ge1}$ be the Tribonacci sequence, defined by $T_1=T_2=1$, $T_3=2$, and $T_n=T_{n-1}+T_{n-2}+T_{n-3}$ for $n\ge4$. In this paper, we study the Tribonacci numbers whose decimal representation is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits, that is, numbers of the shape $\overline{d_1\cdots d_1\,d_2\cdots d_2\,d_1\cdots d_1}$ with $1\le d_1\le9$, $0\le d_2\le9$, $d_1\ne d_2$. We prove that no Tribonacci number is a palindromic concatenation of two distinct repdigits. The proof combines lower bounds for linear forms in logarithms, the Baker-Davenport reduction method, and a finite computational verification.
item.dc:creator: Khady Faye, Bernadette Faye

item.title: $6$ powers of $2$ in the Linnik--Goldbach problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.15784v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linnik's approximation to Goldbach's conjecture concerns the representation of sufficiently large even integers as the sum of two primes and a bounded number of powers of two. We prove that $6$ powers of $2$ suffice unconditionally and that $5$ suffice under the GRH, improving previous works.
item.dc:creator: Huixi Li, Zhixin Liu

item.title: A note on the $p$-adic inhomogeneous Littlewood conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bugeaud, Haynes and Velani (2011) resolved a metric version of the $p$-adic Littlewood conjecture. We establish a fully inhomogeneous generalisation of their result, as well as a partially inhomogeneous generalisation of a result of Harrap and Haynes (2013) in the more general mixed setting.
item.dc:creator: Sam Chow, Owen Jones

item.title: Iwasawa cohomology of pseudorigid families of $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules
item.description: arXiv:2610.15845v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Iwasawa cohomology complex attached to a pseudorigid family of $(\varphi, \Gamma)$-modules and prove coadmissibility of its cohomology groups, perfectness and compatibility with base change. We apply this result to give another proof of perfectness of the Herr complex in pseudorigid family. We also use it to prove perfectness of Selmer complexes and obtain a result on variation of ranks of Selmer groups in analytic family.
item.dc:creator: Yashi Jain

item.title: Nonlinear twists of Rankin-Selberg coefficients in the eigenvalue aspect
item.description: arXiv:2610.15979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $g$ be a fixed primitive Hecke--Maass cusp form, and let $f$ vary with spectral parameter $k_f=K$, at a fixed level and with trivial nebentypus. We study smooth sums of $\lambda_f(n)\lambda_g(n)e(\alpha n^\beta)$ for fixed real $\alpha\ne0$. The crucial input is the smooth spectral second moment of Lau, Liu, and Ye, for which the window length can be taken to be $L=K^{1/3+a}$ for arbitrarily small fixed $a>0$. We show that, for every $\kappa>0$, there is $\beta_0>0$ such that the sum is $O(K^{2/3+\kappa}X^{1/2})$ for $1\le X\le K^2$ and $0<\beta\le\beta_0$. We give a detailed Baire category argument which makes the dependence on the smooth weight uniform through one finite derivative norm. A second argument keeps the phase explicit, applies Voronoi summation and shifted convolution estimates, and gives the numerical bound $O(K^{423/224+(5/7)\beta+\varepsilon})$ at $X=K^2$ for $0<\beta<5/32$.
item.dc:creator: Yangbo Ye

item.title: Zero density in short strips and short-interval bounds toward Hypothesis S
item.description: arXiv:2610.15989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We deduce zero-density estimates in short vertical strips from short-interval moments of globally tempered automorphic $L$-functions, by adapting the large-value estimate of Guth and Maynard and the Type II zero argument of Maynard and Pratt to the framework of Ye and Zhang. For the Riemann zeta function, we obtain $N_\zeta(\sigma;T,T+T^a)\ll T^{15a(1-\sigma)/(3+5\sigma)+\varepsilon}$ for $2/3\le a\le1$ and $7/10\le\sigma\le4/5$. This improves Ye--Zhang's exponent for $7/10<\sigma<4/5$ and localizes Guth--Maynard's density bound to short intervals of ordinates. Through the explicit formula, we apply these estimates to smoothed prime-power sums with phase $\exp(2\pi i\alpha n^\beta)$, for fixed $\alpha\ne0$ and $0<\beta<1$. We obtain explicit power savings over the interval length $K^\delta$ for zeta and, using the earlier cusp-form density bounds, for certain real primitive character twists of self-dual $GL(2)$ cusp forms and self-dual $GL(3)$ Maass cusp forms. The smallest interval thresholds in these three applications are $2/3$, $3/4$, and $5/6$, respectively. We give explicit frequency dependence when $\alpha$ is replaced by $m\alpha$, uniformly for $1\le m\le K^R$ with any fixed $R>0$. The cusp-form applications do not require the Ramanujan conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Yangbo Ye

item.title: On bass orders in division algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.16002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A result by F.-T. Tu dating from 2011 states that the orders in a local matrix algebra of dimension four that can be written as a finite intersection of maximal orders are those having an Eichler Gorenstein closure. In a more recent paper, we gave a similar characterization for orders with a Bass Gorenstein closure. More precisely, we prove that these orders are the ones that can be written as a ghost intersection, i.e., the set of points defined over the base field of an intersection of maximal orders that is defined over a field extension. Although we proved this result only for the local four-dimensional matrix algebra, the statement makes sense also for a local quaternion division algebra, since the latter turns into a matrix algebra when we extend the base field to an even degree extension. In this work, we prove an analog of our previous result in the latter setting.
item.dc:creator: Luis Arenas-Carmona

item.title: Low Lying Zeros of Dedekind Zeta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n_K$, and let $h(K)$ denote the smallest absolute value of the imaginary part of a non-trivial zero of its Dedekind zeta function. In 1979, Hoffstein proved the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.87+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$. In a 1990 survey article, Odlyzko stated without proof that a different kernel in Weil's explicit formula could produce $h(K)\leq 0.54+o(1)$. No further improvement on Hoffstein's $0.87$ threshold accompanied by a published proof has since appeared. We choose a linear kernel and first show that Hoffstein's original parameters already yield the improved constant $0.825$. We then generalise his linear kernel method using Stechkin's trick and prove the unconditional bound $h(K)\leq 0.6+o(1)$ as $n_K\to\infty$, giving the best proved asymptotic bound to date.
item.dc:creator: Timothy S. Trudgian, Sebastian Zuniga-Alterman

item.title: The Multiplicity One Defect and Congruence-Modular Exponent Ratios
item.description: arXiv:2610.16092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a multiplicity one defect that quantitatively measures the failure of multiplicity one for the Jacobian of the Shimura curve \(X^D(M)\) attached to an indefinite rational quaternion algebra of discriminant \(D\) and level \(M\), localized at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra. By constructing a certain lattice inside the local Tate module, we obtain an explicit upper bound for the defect in terms of congruences between eigenforms and the lattice-Tate module discrepancies associated with the individual newforms. We then show that the local ratio between the congruence exponent and the modular exponent of modular abelian varieties attached to newforms is bounded above by the multiplicity one defect. Finally, we examine the relation with the Gorenstein property and give an explicit example at level \(126\) where the local Hecke algebra is Gorenstein even though multiplicity one fails. In this example, we compute the multiplicity one defect to be \(3\), which is also the local congruence--modular exponent ratio.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Masih Hamidi

item.title: Cohen-Lenstra heuristics and vanishing of zeta functions for superelliptic curves over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.16112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a Cohen-Lenstra type result commenting on the distribution of class group structures amongst function fields of superelliptic curves over finite fields. We also prove a result commenting on the sparsity of such superelliptic curves whose zeta functions vanish at a fixed complex number. These results are proven via point-counting techniques on certain Hurwitz schemes generalizing techniques of Ellenberg-Venkatesh-Westerland and Ellenberg-Li-Shusterman. To obtain these point counts, We prove a unitary big monodromy theorem generalizing big monodromy theorems of Yu and Achter-Pries by appealing to an arithmeticity theorem of Venkataramana.
item.dc:creator: Hyun Jong Kim

item.title: Wasserstein rates of all orders for the Sato-Tate law of Kloosterman sums
item.description: arXiv:2610.16169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mu_q$ be the distribution of the normalized Kloosterman sums $\mathrm{Kl}(a;q)$, $a\in\mathbb{F}_q^\times$, and let $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$ be the Sato--Tate law. We prove $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/3}$ for $1\le s\le2$, $W_s(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6-1/(3s)}$ for $2\le s<\infty$, and $W_\infty(\mu_q,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})\ll q^{-1/6}$, answering a question of Kowalski and Untrau. More generally, we bound $W_s(\mu,\mu_{\mathrm{ST}})$ for all $s$ whenever the Chebyshev moments of $\mu$ satisfy bounds of Katz type. For $s=2$ the bound also follows from a smoothing inequality of Borda and Cuenin; for $s>2$ and $s=\infty$ our bounds are stronger. The proof uses the quantile coupling, which arises from Stieltjes sums over two different intervals whose cells are paired so as to balance two measures, and which is optimal for all $s$ simultaneously; an explicit $W_2$ smoothing inequality relative to $\mu_{\mathrm{ST}}$; and a sharp comparison between $W_s$ and the Kolmogorov distance for laws with square-root edges. The last result shows that $q^{-1/6}$ is the best rate for $W_\infty$ obtainable from Niederreiter's discrepancy bound. Numerically, for primes $10^3<p<10^6$, all these distances appear to decay like $p^{-1/2}$.
item.dc:creator: Amir M. Rahimi

item.title: Irreducible components of crystabelline deformation rings: the wildly ramified case
item.description: arXiv:2610.16225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p\geq11$ be a prime, and let $\bar\rho:\Gal(\bar\QQ_p/\QQ_p)\rightarrow\GL_2(\bar\FF_p)$ be a reducible and very generic representation. In this paper, we use ghost series \cite{Lghost2} to study the irreducible components of Kisin's potentially crystalline deformation rings of $\bar\rho$. For wildly ramified principal series inertial types and arbitrary regular Hodge--Tate weights, we distinguish the components by the crystabelline slopes on their generic fibers and determine the total number of irreducible components. Combining this with an explicit formula for the total Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber obtained from the Breuil--M\'ezard conjecture, we compute the Hilbert--Samuel multiplicity of the special fiber of each component. Every such multiplicity is one when $\bar\rho$ is non-split, and is either one or two when $\bar\rho$ is split, according to whether the generic fiber of the corresponding component parametrizes reducible or irreducible Galois representations.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei An

item.title: A Lean formalisation of the disproof of Ramaekers's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16323v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe Redhill, a Lean formalisation of the major results in H\"olzl, Kleine and Stephan's "Improved Lower Bounds for Strong $n$-Conjectures" (arXiv:2409.13439). Design decisions regarding types and data structures are justified as enabling canonical versions of the paper's claims, and from there the most direct proofs of said claims. The formalisation process also uncovered many errors, omissions and optimisation opportunities in the informal proof, all of which are addressed in the final library. Although Redhill is meant to stand alone, a few lemmas were upstreamed to the primary Lean mathematics library mathlib. We discuss the tension between upstreaming and leaving lemmas in separate libraries. Unlike many other contemporary formalisation projects, Redhill was completed without any assistance from large language models (LLMs). We compare our work with LLM-assisted projects, in particular an extension of arXiv:2409.13439 to $n=4$, aiming to establish design and style guidelines that define good Lean formalisations.
item.dc:creator: Jeremy Tan

item.title: Dynamical generalizations of the two-point Chowla conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.16394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1965, Chowla conjectured that the values of the Liouville function become asymptotically uncorrelated at consecutive natural numbers. Recently, the two-point case is resolved by OpenAI. In 2026, Charamaras and Richter conjectured a generalization of the Chowla conjecture to the asymptotic independence of the consecutive prime Omega functions. In this article, we prove the two-point case of their conjecture. As a consequence, we obtain a dynamical generalization of the two-point Chowla conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Biao Wang, Shaoyun Yi

item.title: Stable reduction and large Nielsen orbits on generalized Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish lower bounds on the orbit cardinalities of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ on the $\mathbb{F}_p$-points of the generalized Markoff surfaces given by $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 - xyz = \tau+2$. We show that outside of the reductions of a certain exceptional finite set of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points found by Dubrovin and Mazzocco, every orbit has cardinality $\ge p$. Together with a recent result of Nathaniel Kingsbury-Neuschotz, this establishes, for all but finitely many primes $p$, the classification conjectures of McCullough-Wanderley (2013), and gives a complete classification of the connected components of the Hurwitz stack of $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of elliptic curves, only branched above the origin. This extends earlier work of Bourgain-Gamburd-Sarnak and the author in the Markoff case $\tau = -2$. Our method studies certain noncongruence modular curves attached to a $\text{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$-orbit. These modular curves parametrize elliptic curves with a $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-cover. We use this moduli interpretation to show that the noncongruence modular curves involved have bad reduction, as a cover of the $j$-line, at some place above $p$. This implies that the degree of the cover is $\ge p$, which translates into the desired bound on orbits. Key inputs include a result of Bouw-Wewers on bad reduction of three-point $\text{PSL}(2,\mathbb{F}_p)$-covers of the projective line, and the general stable reduction theory of Henrio, Obus, Raynaud, and Wewers.
item.dc:creator: William Y. Chen

item.title: Hecke modules associated to certain even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $\mathbf{N^2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider Hecke modules of orthogonal modular forms attached to definite even ternary lattices of half-discriminant $N^2$, where $N > 1$ is odd and square-free. We prove explicit Jacquet-Langlands style correspondences with spaces of classical modular forms (in the spirit of Birch and Hein-Tornaria-Voight). This is done by applying sequences of Watson-style transformations that reduce the discriminant while preserving the adelic orthogonal group.
item.dc:creator: Samadrito Bhattacharyya, Giovanna De Lauri, Dan Fretwell

item.title: Bounded continued fractions and quadratic orders in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the least periods and multiplier orders in two constructions of Mercat for continued fractions with bounded partial quotients. Our main explicit result concerns a family in $\Q(\sqrt{127})$ with partial quotients at most $4$. For every integer $j\geq1$, we prove that its primitive period has length $92j+2$ and its multiplier order has conductor $y_{4j}/4$, where $(4730624+419775\sqrt{127})^k=x_k+y_k\sqrt{127}$. The totally positive unit group of this order has index $4j$ in that of the maximal order. These exact formulas give divisor-sum lower bounds at fixed traces and a lower bound of order $(\log X)^2$ for the number of bounded continued fractions with discriminant at most $X$. We also prove a primitive-period refinement of Mercat's palindromic construction. Combining this refinement with Hensley's counting theorem gives, for every $m\geq2$ and $\eta>0$, at least $X^{\delta_m/2-\eta}$ quadratic fields, up to a positive constant, that admit infinitely many purely periodic continued fractions with partial quotients at most $m$. Here $\delta_m$ is the Hausdorff dimension of the corresponding continued fraction Cantor set.
item.dc:creator: Shirali Kadyrov, Aiken Kazin, Alibek Orynbassar, Nurdaulet Shynarbek

item.title: The Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16562v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the maximal length of a minimal zero-sum sequence over $\left[\!\left[ -m,m \right]\!\right]^d$ having a support of size $d+1$. When $d=2$, we find the exact value of this maximal length for all $m \ge 2$, as well as the exact structure of all extremal sequences for this problem. When $d=3$, we obtain lower and upper bounds that asymptotically match each other as $m$ tends to infinity. This allows us to improve on the best known lower bounds for the Davenport constant of low-dimensional boxes.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Girard, Alain Plagne

item.title: The ring of values of $E$-functions is not a field
item.description: arXiv:2610.16603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathbf{E}$ be the ring of values taken at algebraic points by $E$-functions. The exponential function and the Bessel function $J_0$ are classical examples of $E$-functions. We prove that $\mathbf{E}$ is not a field. More precisely, we prove that it is neither noetherian nor factorial, and construct non-units of $\mathbf{E}$ explicity, including $e+1$, $J_0(1)$, and ${}_1F_1(a;b;1)$ for rational parameters $a$ and $b$ such that $0
item.dc:creator: St\'ephane Fischler (LMO), Tanguy Rivoal (IF)

item.title: Sparse Lifts of q-Linearized Permutation Polynomials with Explicit Inverses
item.description: arXiv:2610.16619v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a higher unit-torus lift from q-linearized permutation polynomials over Fqn to generally nonlinear sparse permutation polynomials over Fqns. The construction preserves compositional inverses: if a linearized polynomials and its inverse have coefficients (ai) and (Ai), then the lifted polynomial and its inverse have the same coefficients. As a consequence, we obtain nonlinear binomial lifts whose inverses are again binomials in the two-dimensional case, including an explicit inverse for a binomial family over Fq4. The three dimensional specialization yields permutation trinomials whose compositional inverses are again trinomials, together with explicit involution criteria and examples.
item.dc:creator: Yi Li

item.title: Pointwise improvement of the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an upper bound for the error term in the higher rank hyperbolic lattice counting problem for ${\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{Z})}$. Blomer and Lutsko achieved recently a significant improvement of previous known results by Duke--Rudnick--Sarnak and Gorodnik--Nevo--Yehoshua. We deduce an improved upper bound for the error which holds for almost all pairs $z,w \in {\hbox{SL}(n, \mathbb{R})}$. We also derive a $\Omega$-result for the error term, in the spirit of Rudnick--Phillips.
item.dc:creator: Dimitrios Chatzakos, Panagiotis Dimakis, Christos Katsivelos

item.title: On Solvable Automorphism Groups of Function Fields over Finite Fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.16751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Hurwitz bound gives a linear upper bound for automorphism groups of algebraic curves in characteristic zero, whereas algebraic curves in positive characteristic can have much larger automorphism groups. In this article, we firstly investigate the solvable subgroups and $p$-subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ where $p=\operatorname{char}(\mathbb{F}_q)$ and $F/\mathbb{F}_q$ is a function field of genus $g_F\ge2$ with full constant field $\mathbb{F}_q$. We prove that there are explicit constants $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}$ and $C_q^{(p)}$, depending only on $q$, such that, for every solvable subgroup $G\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$ and every $p$-subgroup $P\le\operatorname{Aut}(F/\mathbb{F}_q)$, \[ |G|\le C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}(g_F-1), \qquad |P|\le C_q^{(p)}(g_F-1). \] In particular, one may take $C_q^{(\mathrm{sol})}=12q^2(q-1)$ for $q\ge4$ and $C_q^{(p)}=5q$ for every $q$. In the second part of this article , we give the asymptotic lower bounds for solvable automorphism groups. For every $q$ there is an explicit constant $L_q>0$ and a sequence of function fields $F_i/\mathbb{F}_q$ with $g_{F_i}\to\infty$, together with solvable subgroups $G_i\le\operatorname{Aut}(F_i/\mathbb{F}_q)$, such that \[ |G_i|\ge L_q(g_{F_i}-1). \] For $q\ge5$ one may take $L_q=2q(q-1)/(q-2)$. If $q=r^2$ with $r\ge3$, an unramified tower construction over the Hermitian curve gives the stronger choice $L_q=2r^3(r-1)/(r-2)$. Moreover, as an application of our tower construction above, we improve the lower bound of Ma and Xing to $B_q\ge 2(q-1)/(q-2)$ for $q\ge 5$. As another application, we extend our method for bounding solvable automorphism groups to $p$-solvable subgroups, obtaining explicit linear bounds in terms of the genus.
item.dc:creator: Henning Stichtenoth, Chaoping Xing, Zugan Xing

item.title: Automorphisms and canonical forms of integer lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.16753v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We improve the Plesken--Souvignier algorithm for computing automorphism groups and isometries of positive definite integer quadratic lattices by exploiting characteristic sublattices and refining vector enumeration. For lattices with roots, we also use the Weyl group to accelerate the computation of canonical forms. Experiments with concrete implementations demonstrate substantial speedups and show that canonical forms can be computed at a cost comparable to that of computing automorphism groups.
item.dc:creator: Simon Brandhorst, Tommy Hofmann

item.title: The WZ pair and finite congruences
item.description: arXiv:2610.16844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a meromorphic Wilf--Zeilberger pair for the hypergeometric series for \(3\ln 2\), completing the WZ proof left open by Guillera and Rogers. The same pair yields a one-parameter identity and, after a half-integer shift and differentiation, an inverse-binomial series for \(\zeta(3)\). We also study the finite truncations of the logarithmic series. For every prime \(p\ge 5\), we prove that the lower truncation is congruent to \(q_p(2)-1\) modulo \(p\), while the upper truncation is congruent to \(-\frac{7}{16}p^2B_{p-3}\) modulo \(p^3\). The proofs combine the WZ method with terminating hypergeometric identities, the Pfaff--Saalsch\"utz identity, and classical congruences for harmonic sums.
item.dc:creator: Xiang Chen, Junyan Liu, Hengfei Lu

item.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.
item.dc:creator: Jingxuan Geng

item.title: Distribution of central values of Hecke $L$-functions of $n$-th order characters
item.description: arXiv:2610.17144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a one-sided central limit theorem for $\log |L(\tfrac 12,\chi)|$ in a thin family of $n$-th order Hecke characters, for $n \geq 3$. The proof combines the method of Radziwi{\l}{\l} and Soundararajan with a recent asymptotic formula of Diaconu, Ion, Pa\c{s}ol, and Popa for the twisted second moment with a power-saving error term. We also obtain upper bounds of the conjectured order of magnitude for the $2k$-th moments for $0< k< 1$.
item.dc:creator: Lewis McGoldrick

item.title: A Half-Constant Upper Bound for Chowla's Cosine Problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.17160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let lambda(n) denote the infimum of -min_x sum_{a in A} cos(ax) over all sets A of n positive integers. While the classical Sidon-difference construction yields lambda(n) <= (1 + o(1))sqrt(n)/2, we construct sets achieving a leading constant of 1/2: lambda(n) <= (1/2)sqrt(n) + O(n^(1/4)sqrt(log n)), establishing limsup_{n->infinity} lambda(n)/sqrt(n) <= 1/2. This construction combines a two-sided Sidon square identity, a Singer difference set, a Fejer-kernel majorant, a parity-biased deletion, and an exact-cardinality probabilistic selection. We also provide an L^4 criterion and a multiplicity bound constraining any construction with a smaller leading constant. In the opposite direction, we incorporate the L^1 norm into Bedert's boundary estimate with an explicit constant, yielding two lower bounds for f_A(x) = sum_{a in A} cos(ax): (1) -min f_A >= cn^(1/4) for every n-element set A subset of [1, Cn]; and (2) (-min f_A)^3 ||f_A||_1^2 >= cn for every n-element set A subset of N. The second bound recovers the 1/5 exponent of Bedert and Shankar and improves it whenever ||f_A||_1 is small relative to -min f_A. Numerical values of the construction are reported up to |A| = 25,440.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Bu, Fayzan Khan, Hyunjun Yi, Atharv Jha, Vihaan Vajpeyi, Ishaan Chandupatla, Madhav Nagpal

item.title: Holonomic sequences arising from meromorphic modular forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.17240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a systematic framework for constructing holonomic recurrences from meromorphic modular forms. Its central ingredient is a modular analogue of creative telescoping, which turns finite-dimensional quotients of spaces of meromorphic modular forms into explicit recurrence operators. This provides a common explanation for several previously isolated examples: it recovers Ap\'ery's recurrence, Beukers' modular constructions and Zagier's seven sporadic recurrences. The framework also produces a large collection of new examples across different weights and groups. The modular origin of these sequences also confers them with non-trivial arithmetic properties, such as denominator bounds, irrationality statements, and $p$-adic congruences.
item.dc:creator: Kam Cheong Au

item.title: An Enhanced Higher Green's Function on the Modular Curve
item.description: arXiv:2610.17258v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The higher Green's functions $G_{k/2}(z,w)$ on the modular curve are real-valued eigenfunctions of the hyperbolic Laplacian in each variable, with logarithmic singularities along the diagonal. Gross and Zagier conjectured that their values at CM points, after multiplication by suitable powers of the discriminants, are logarithms of absolute values of algebraic numbers. The conjecture was proved by Li, Bruinier, and Yang. Mellit proposed a complex refinement of this conjecture, predicting that the normalized CM values of a complex lift of the Green function are logarithms of algebraic numbers modulo periods. For $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ and $k\in{4,6,8,10,14}$, we follow Zagier's construction of CM invariants from Eichler integrals of the Eisenstein series $E_4$. By applying Maass raising operators in both variables to a normalized iterated Eichler integral of a Bergman-type kernel, we obtain a complex-valued extension $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet(z,w)$ whose real part is a constant multiple of $G_{k/2}(z,w)$. We study the normalized CM values of $\mathcal G_{k/2}^\bullet$ and describe their dependence on the choice of representatives of quadratic form classes. In particular, we show that replacing the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable by an equivalent one changes the exponential of the normalized value only by a root of unity. We also prove the algebraicity of these exponentials in the special case where the second CM point is $w_*=(1+i\sqrt d)/2$, with $d>3$ and $d\equiv3\pmod4$, and the class of the quadratic form corresponding to the first variable is equal to its inverse.
item.dc:creator: Nina Sakharova

item.title: Likely and unlikely ramification of algebraic points on curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.17262v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper initiates the study of arithmetic properties of closed points of arbitrary degree on curves. We show that a pointless curve of rank $0$ can have only finitely many cyclic degree $\ell$ points for all sufficiently large primes $\ell$. More generally, we show that the residue fields of points on curves of genus at least $2$ and rank $0$ are often biased away from total ramification. The proof technique illuminates a natural intermediate conjecture between the Manin--Mumford conjecture and the Zilber--Pink conjecture for self-products of abelian varieties. This intermediate conjecture implies analogous results for other splitting profiles.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Viray, Isabel Vogt

item.title: Denominators in the Farey Sequence, the Stern Sequence, and the Frobenius Problem with Relatively Prime Multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2610.17267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Frobenius problem asks, given two positive, relatively prime integers $a$ and $b$, what is the maximum integer that cannot be expressed as a linear combination of $a,b$ using non-negative coefficients? This problem is resolved. However, if we add the restriction that the coefficients themselves must also be relatively prime, we create an open problem with connections to the Stern and Farey sequences and the Jacobsthal function. We prove that under this new restriction, a maximum inexpressible integer still always exists, and explore its values and properties as functions of $a,b$.
item.dc:creator: Grace Natalie Jaffe

item.title: Arithmetic jet spaces and the unramified Zilber--Pink conjecture for subvarieties of abelian varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.17325v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how the methods of delta geometry can be used to bound the degree of points in the Zilber--Pink locus of a subvariety of an abelian variety, if the varieties are defined over a number field and we restrict to points with bounded ramification at a fixed prime.
item.dc:creator: Netan Dogra, Arnab Saha

item.title: Higher derivatives of the Gram function
item.description: arXiv:2610.17349v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nonlinear phenomenon of the asymptotics of higher-order derivatives of the Gram function $t_u$. We also prove the uniform distribution and continuous uniform distribution modulo one of $t^n_u$ for $n = 1, 2, \dots$. We use AI to formalize our proofs in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Marius Dundulis, Ram\=unas Garunk\v{s}tis, Antanas Laurin\v{c}ikas, Raivydas \v{S}im\.enas

item.title: Roth's theorem on weighted projective lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.17589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let ${\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}$ be the weighted projective line with coprime weights ${\mathfrak q}=(q_0,q_1)$ and $L=q_0q_1$. The weighted Veronese map $\Phi\colon {\mathbb P}^1_{\mathfrak q}\to {\mathbb P}^1$ satisfies $h\circ\Phi=L\,{\mathfrak s}$. Pulling back Roth's theorem gives the optimal exponent $2L$ for the full rational orbit set. For points represented by coprime integral coordinates, counting suggests the smaller exponent $q_0+q_1$. We formulate this as a conjecture and prove an $S$-adic radical form under the $abc$ conjecture. For ${\mathfrak q}=(2,3)$ the resulting inequality at the target $[1:1]$ is the coprime Hall-type inequality, and Danilov--Elkies examples show that the exponent $5$ is sharp. We also prove the expected exponent unconditionally over characteristic-zero function fields for constant targets and polynomial approximants, and for almost every real target. A weighted $abc$ formulation is introduced; in signature $(3,2)$ finitely many coefficient pairs are equivalent to $abc$, and weighted Belyi maps transfer this input to arbitrary algebraic targets. Applications include a pullback form of Schmidt's subspace theorem, weighted Thue inequalities, and a counterexample to a naive weighted rescaling of Roth's index construction.
item.dc:creator: Sajad Salami

item.title: The local structure of refined class groups in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.17649v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give an explicit local description of ray class refinements in cyclotomic Iwasawa theory. For distinct primes $p\geq5$ and $\ell$, and even $2\leq k\leq p-3$, we prove that the $\omega^{1-k}$-component of the $p$-primary ray class group of $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_p)$, with squarefree modulus supported above $\ell$, is nonzero if and only if $p\mid\ell(1-\ell^k)B_k$. In the cyclotomic tower, we determine the local modules and their correction modulo the diagonal global Tate module, obtaining an explicit determinant formula. Their Frobenius Euler factors, combined with the Mazur--Wiles theorem, yield a ray class form of the Iwasawa main conjecture for nonexceptional odd characters. We also obtain exact class number valuation comparisons at every layer, including those before stabilization, recover Finat's formula for $\ell=2$, and deduce refined $\mu$-vanishing from Ferrero--Washington. The cyclotomic character explains the Wieferich exception, while existing Eisenstein congruence theorems connect the divisibility criteria with prime-level Ramanujan-style congruences.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: Simultaneously preperiodic points and colliding orbits for families of polynomials in characteristic $p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.17650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k=\overline{\mathbb{F}}_p$ and let $f\in k[X]$ be a polynomial of degree at least $2$ such that $f-f(0)$ is non-additive. For $\alpha,\beta$ in an algebraically closed extension $L$ of $k$, we prove that there are infinitely many $\lambda\in L$ for which both points are preperiodic under $f(X)+\lambda$ if and only if $\alpha,\beta\in k$ or $f(\beta)-f(\alpha)\in E_f$. Here $E_f=\{c\in G_f:(f-f(0))^n(c)\in G_f\text{ for every }n\ge0\}$, where $G_f=\{c\in k : f(X+c)-f(X)\in k\}$. We also provide a necessary and sufficient criterion for the corresponding colliding orbits set to be infinite.
item.dc:creator: Jungin Lee, GyeongHyeon Nam

item.title: A sharp lower bound for the sextic large sieve
item.description: arXiv:2610.17675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a matching lower bound for the sextic large sieve over the Eisenstein integers in an unbalanced range, with both indices restricted to squarefree ideals. Let $\Xi_6(A,B)$ denote the squared operator norm of the sextic residue-character matrix with row and column norms at most $A$ and $B$, respectively, outside a fixed finite set of primes containing those above $6$. For every fixed $0<\delta<3/11$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove $\Xi_6(A,B)\gg_{\delta,\varepsilon}(AB)^{-\varepsilon}A^{5/6}B^{1/3}$ for $B^{16/11+\delta}\le A\le B^{2-\delta}$. Consequently, the full-cutoff norm satisfies $\Xi_6(X,X)\gg_\varepsilon X^{17/16-\varepsilon}$. The main difficulty is to preserve the large second moment supplied by Gauss sums when the column moduli are restricted to be squarefree. We prove a second-moment formula uniform in the prime exclusions and character twists arising from M\"obius inversion, and use it to show that the squarefree projection retains a positive proportion of the original moment. A separate argument combining cubic and sextic large-sieve bounds then transfers the lower bound to squarefree rows.
item.dc:creator: Yuanda Xu, Hejian Sang

item.title: Yau's number-theoretic conjecture and sharp spectral bounds for quantum harmonic oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17704v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Yau's number-theoretic conjecture on positive integral points in real right simplices in every dimension $n\ge3$, and apply the resulting sharp polynomial bound to quantum harmonic oscillators. The lattice-point bound holds for every choice of positive real intercepts for which the count is nonzero, with equality precisely when all intercepts equal the same integer. For oscillators in dimensions $n\ge3$, we obtain explicit upper bounds for eigenvalue counts and spectral remainders for arbitrary positive frequencies at every threshold at or above the lowest eigenvalue. For frequencies with rational ratios in dimensions $n\ge2$, an additional lattice coordinate and interpolation give bounds for energy sums, or first Riesz means, at every threshold. When all frequencies are equal (the isotropic case), the oscillator attains these bounds: the counting bound is exact at its energy levels, and interpolation on its natural energy grid recovers the energy sum at every threshold. In three dimensions, the exact formula displays the periodic contribution associated with the resonance discussed by Fefferman and Seco. The proof builds on the slicing method of Yau and Zhang. Arithmetic and geometric consequences include explicit bounds for smooth numbers and lattice-point discrepancies.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Hao Zuo

item.title: A recurrence in logarithmic M\"obius sums with coprimality conditions via Euler--Maclaurin
item.description: arXiv:2610.17720v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a recurrence for logarithmically weighted M\"obius sums by combining M\"obius inversion with the Euler--Maclaurin summation formula. Consequently, starting from estimates of orders zero, one and two, we obtain polynomial approximations for these sums for every nonnegative integer exponent of $\log$. We then extend these estimates to sums with coprimality conditions via a convolution identity and to sums weighted by the reciprocal of the sum-of-divisors function. We also establish the nonnegativity of the latter sums for every positive integer logarithmic order, proving that they never change sign.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Zuniga-Alterman

item.title: Fine structure of even Galois deformation rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.17865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every even Galois representation in a family of prime conductor $\ell$, we prove that if $k \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is maximal such that \[\ell \equiv 1 \bmod 3^k\] then the even mod $3$ deformation ring $R_S \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_3} \mathbb{F}_3$ of level $S=\{\ell,3\}$ does not have a quotient isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_3[T]/(T^{2+3^{k-1}})$. As a corollary, we deduce that the global even deformation rings $R_S$ are finite and flat in the category of $\mathbb{Z}_3$-modules.
item.dc:creator: Peter Vang Uttenthal

item.title: A generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values via Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation
item.description: arXiv:2610.17957v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a generating function identity for finite and symmetric multiple zeta values using Dougall's bilateral ${}_2H_2$ summation formula. As an application, we prove a restricted sum formula in which the parity of each component of the index is prescribed. We also derive a generating function identity for finite multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{A}}(\{1,2\}^n)$ and symmetric multiple zeta values $\zeta^{}_{\mathcal{S}}(\{1,2\}^n)$, thereby proving Kaneko's conjecture for finite multiple zeta values and its symmetric analogue.
item.dc:creator: Takumi Maesaka, Masataka Ono

item.title: On Berndt-Straub conjectures about zeros of generalized Ramanujan polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.18065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We settle two conjectures of Berndt and Straub asserting that all nonzero zeros of the generalized Ramanujan polynomials $R_k(x;\chi,\psi)$ and $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ lie on the unit circle for real nonprincipal Dirichlet characters. We prove their conjecture for $R_k$. For $S_{2n}$, we prove that at most four nonzero zeros lie off the unit circle, all purely imaginary. If $\chi_{163}=\left(\frac{\cdot}{163}\right)$ is the primitive quadratic character modulo $163$, then $S_6(x;\chi_{163},\chi_{163})$ has four exceptional zeros, showing that this bound is sharp. This disproves the second conjecture and establishes that the `Riemann hypothesis for period polynomials' can fail for Eisenstein newforms. Further, we introduce a transcendental invariant whose sign determines whether exceptional zeros of $S_{2n}(x;\chi,\chi)$ occur in all sufficiently large degrees, and show that these zeros converge to transcendental limits off the unit circle. For primitive odd characters, we relate this invariant and these limits to Fekete polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Siddhi Pathak

item.title: A certified classical-strip comparison for the de Bruijn-Newman constant
item.description: arXiv:2610.18214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give a directed comparison beginning with the classical zero strip \(\lvert\Ima z\rvert\le1\) for the de Bruijn--Newman heat deformation. Under explicitly stated complete model-to-function source, localisation and global contact premises, translated-probe estimates imply \[ \Lambda\le\frac{148611789321711}{10^{15}} =0.148611789321711<0.148612. \] The construction uses Raymond's finite source data and 57 fixed translated kernels, independently checked by rational Bernstein certificates. An explicit finite Weyl estimate improves the positive first-head tail and its centred logarithmic moment. A centred cone transfer retains the original physical error allowances, exceptional debit and additive cone reserve, and charges the change in existing phase-surplus credits. Directed tail enclosures are regenerated at 192 and 256 bits; a separate exact-rational auditor accepts all 19,023 comparison steps. The controlled decrease from the complete two-source comparison is \(0.000021760452379\). We also prove a compatible matched logarithmic tail transfer and identify the finite requirements for stronger exponent pairs. A supplementary section records Raymond's ceiling below \(0.116398\) under the distinct \(7/8\) zero-free hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Michel Planat

item.title: Counting matrices with given characteristic polynomial
item.description: arXiv:2610.18226v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a monic polynomial of degree $n$ with integer coefficients. We use Fourier analysis to prove a new upper bound on the number of $n\times n$ matrices with characteristic polynomial $f$ and integer entries in $[-T,T]$, as $T\to \infty$. The implied constant in our bound only depends on $n$ and is otherwise uniform in $f$. Our bound improves on recent work of Habegger, Ostafe and Shparlinski for $n\geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Tim Browning, Fabian Gundlach, Will Sawin

item.title: Higher rank elliptic sieve via CM endomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.18281v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A theorem of Landau and Ramanujan states that almost all integers are not sums of two squares (when ordered by their absolute value). Equivalently, almost all integers are not norms from the Gaussian rationals $\mathbb{Q}(i)$. In this paper, we prove a version of this norm result for elliptic curves $E$. Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over a number field $K$ with complex multiplication, such that $K$ contains the endomorphism ring of $E$. For a fixed non-torsion point $P \in E(K)$ and an abelian extension $L/K$, we show that subject to a technical condition, the $y$-coordinate of almost all multiples of $P$ does not belong to the norm group of $L$. The proof is an adaptation of an argument of Bhakta et al. , whose main tools are elliptic divisibility sequences and a sieve technique known as the elliptic sieve. To account for the points in $E(K)$ arising from the additional endomorphisms, we apply the elliptic sieve to elliptic nets, a higher-rank generalisation of elliptic divisibility sequences. This approach demonstrates the possibility of applying the elliptic sieve to $\mathbb{Z}$--linear combination of points on elliptic curves and the usefulness of elliptic nets to counting problems on elliptic curves.
item.dc:creator: Hang Lok Edison Au-Yeung

item.title: Untrodden pathways in the study of partitions with parts separated by parity
item.description: arXiv:2610.18319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a partition function with parts separated by parity from a family of partition functions introduced by Andrews in 2019. We first show that its generating function admit representation in terms of mock modular forms of weight $3/2$. We then initiate a study of smallest-part partition function analogues of partitions with parts separated by parity, which, to the best of our knowledge, has not previously been investigated in the literature. We show that the generating functions of these smallest-part partition functions are likewise expressible in terms of mock modular forms, mock Maass theta functions and Zagier's $q$-series $H(q)$, which he describes as a ``half-derivative of the Dedekind eta-function". Our study also leads to new combinatorial interpretations of the coefficients of the aforementioned mock modular form, function $\sigma^*(q)$, and mock theta functions $\psi(q)$ and $A(q)$ in terms of odd Ferrers graphs. Moreover, we provide a quantum $q$-series identity involving Ramanujan's famous $\sigma(q)$ function. We also derive the leading asymptotic term of one of these partition functions, whose generating function we first express in terms of $\sigma^*(q)$.
item.dc:creator: Nargish Punia, Rahul Kumar

item.title: A Combinatorial Proof of Partition Identities for the Number of Distinct Part Sizes
item.description: arXiv:2610.18371v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1984, Bressoud and Subbarao established an interesting weighted partition identity connecting the partition function and the divisor function. Recently, the first author, jointly with Bhoria, Eyyunni, and Maji, extended the work of Bressoud and Subbarao and obtained the following analogous weighted partition identity. For any $n \in \mathbb{N}$, they obtained \begin{equation*} p^{(2)}(n) = \sum_{\pi \in \mathcal{D}(n)} (-1)^{ \# (\pi) }s(\pi) \left( \ell(\pi) - s(\pi) \right). \end{equation*} In the present paper, we provide a combinatorial proof of the above identity and extend the result for $p^{(k)}(n)$, where $p^{(k)}(n)$ denotes the number of partitions of $n$ into exactly $k$ distinct part sizes.
item.dc:creator: Archit Agarwal, Meghali Garg
