item.title: On Permutations Whose Adjacent-Sum Reciprocals Sum to One
item.description: arXiv:2610.18431v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give a constructive proof that for any integer n>7 (resp. n>6), the numbers 1,2,...,n can be arranged in a circle (resp. in a line) such that the sum of the reciprocals of all adjacent sums equals 1. The above conjecture was originally posed by Zhi-Wei Sun. Partitioning the integers according to n mod 12 into nine residue classes, we prove a recursive proposition and inductively construct new examples. Main lemmas and propositions in introduction are proved in Section 2. The rest of the cases are handled by explicit constructions in appendix.
item.dc:creator: Jinggao Ai, Dingsheng Hu, Junmin Yan

item.title: Some applications of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis to class groups and small generators of number fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.18491v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an effective version of the Chebotarev density theorem, conditional on the quasi-Riemann hypothesis for the Dedekind zeta function. Drawing on recent breakthroughs of OpenAI and Cureton--Thorner, we make unconditional the Ellenberg--Venkatesh bounds on $\ell$-torsion in class groups of number fields and extend an averaged result of Lemke Oliver--Smith to arbitrary families of degree-$d$-fields. Further applications are given to the least prime splitting and to small generators in number fields.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Frei, Efthymios Sofos, Martin Widmer

item.title: Linking numbers and special differential characters in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18503v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct non-holomorphic Siegel modular forms whose coefficients encode linking numbers in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds of simplest type. Our proofs rely on an improved understanding of the transgression forms appearing in Kudla--Millson theory, and along the way we establish some structural properties including in particular their expected current equations.
item.dc:creator: Mads Bjerge Christensen

item.title: Wendt's determinant and finiteness of prime characteristics for permutation binomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.18584v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $f(X)=X^r(X^s+a)\in\mathbb F_{p^m}[X]$, with $m,r,s\geqslant1$ and $a\in\mathbb F_{p^m}^\times$, put $g=\gcd(s,p^m-1)$. We prove that, for each fixed $g$, only finitely many prime characteristics $p$ admit such permutation binomials, even as $m,r,s,a$ vary. If $6\nmid g$, every such $p$ divides Wendt's determinant $W_g=\operatorname{Res}_X(X^g-1,(X+1)^g-1)$, which is nonzero. When $6\mid g$, this determinant vanishes; inverse power sums and iterated resultants yield an explicit nonzero integer divisible by every such $p>2g+1$. We determine the exact admissible characteristics for $1\leqslant g\leqslant10$, obtain a further divisibility condition over prime fields, and show that in prime fields $g=11$ occurs precisely when $p=23$.
item.dc:creator: Zhichao Tang, Xiang Fan

item.title: Geometric bounds on norms of signed indecomposable integers
item.description: arXiv:2610.18737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish bounds on the norm of signed indecomposable integers in totally real number fields, via a geometric argument. We also improve the bound on the norm of totally positive indecomposable integers in real quadratic fields by Tinkov\'a and Voutier.
item.dc:creator: Siu Hang Man, Zden\v{e}k Pezlar, Pavlo Yatsyna

item.title: Counting quaternion extensions by multi-heights
item.description: arXiv:2610.18815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a case of a conjecture of Gundlach on the number of Galois extensions over $\QQ$ with bounded multi-invariants for the group $G=Q_8$. We also obtain results when imposing local conditions at the wildly ramified place. As an application, we prove asymptotics for the number of $Q_8$-extensions with bounded product of ramified primes.
item.dc:creator: Willem Hansen

item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}

item.title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperk\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.14243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperk\"ahler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.
item.dc:creator: Eva Bayer-Fluckiger, Stevell Muller, Matthias Sch\"utt

item.title: A series with a Cantorval set of subsums and ratio of consecutive terms tending to $1/2$ (the second Jones problem)
item.description: arXiv:2610.14251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The second Jones problem (2011) consists in determining whether there exists a convergent positive series for which the ratio of consecutive terms has a limit and the set of subsums is a Cantorval; in the survey by G{\l}{\k a}b and Prus-Wi\'sniowski (2026) this problem is included in the list of open problems. In this paper, a family of such series is constructed explicitly as combinations of blocks of the form $\frac{2^k-1}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-1}}{2^t} + \frac{2^{k-2}}{2^t} + \cdots + \frac{2}{2^t}$, where $t$ is the index of the last term of the block in the series and $k\ge2$ is the length of the block. For each series of the family it is proved that its set of subsums contains an interval and is not a finite union of closed intervals, and hence is a Cantorval. The proof relies on mixed-radix numerical systems with a redundant alphabet and uses an idea of Guthrie and Nymann (1988). If the lengths of the blocks tend to infinity, then the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms of such series is $\tfrac{1}{2}$, which, by a result of Jones, is the only possible value of the limit for which the set of subsums of a series can be a Cantorval. Thus, an affirmative answer to the second Jones problem is obtained.
item.dc:creator: Mykola Pratsiovytyi, Yaroslav Vynnyshyn, Oleh Vynnyshyn

item.title: Schauder and Riesz Bases for Higher-Dimensional Lebesgue Spaces Inspired by ReLU Neural Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14266v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the role of piecewise linear functions in ReLU neural networks, we study systems of dilated functions in the Lebesgue spaces $L_q([0,1]^d)$, $q\in(1,\infty)$. For a sequence $\tau\in\ell_1$ we consider the operator $T_\tau g(x)=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \tau_k g(kx)$ and the function system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ obtained by applying it to the trigonometric system. We show that $\tau\mapsto T_\tau$ is an isomorphism of algebras from $\ell_1$ with the Dirichlet convolution as multiplication onto an algebra of operators and connect the inverse of $T_\tau$ to the inverse of $\tau$ with respect to the Dirichlet convolution. We give explicit conditions on $\tau$, under which the resulting system $\mathcal Z^\tau$ is a Schauder basis of $L_q([0,1]^d)$ and, for $q=2$, a Riesz basis for which we estimate the Riesz constants in terms of $\tau$. We characterise the Riesz bases of this type in terms of a sequence space of Dirichlet convolution multipliers, and we treat mixed systems of cosine and sine functions with different sequences. Finally, we apply these results to the system generated by two piecewise linear functions inspired by ReLU networks and improve the known lower Riesz constant to $2/3$, independently of the dimension.
item.dc:creator: Julian Billner, Cornelia Schneider

item.title: Lattices with Large Kissing Number from Local Density
item.description: arXiv:2610.14380v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\kappa_p(n)$ denote the maximum kissing number of a lattice $\mathcal{L} \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. We prove that $\kappa_p(n) \geq 2^{\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$ for all $p\ge 1$ and that $\kappa_p(n) \geq \Omega(\alpha_p^n)$ for all $p > 2$, where $\alpha_p > 1$ is a constant depending only on $p$. In particular, our former result improves on the previously best known lower bound of $\kappa_2(n) \geq 2^{\Theta(\log^2 n)}$ for the $\ell_2$ kissing number, which has stood for over $60$ years. (In concurrent and independent work, Laarhoven and Kominers [arXiv, 2026] showed a similar lower bound on $\kappa_2(n)$ using similar techniques.) In fact, our lower bounds follow from efficient (randomized) constructions of lattices with large kissing number. Our results use a general construction of lattices with large kissing number. Specifically, we show a simple equivalence between such lattices and a new object that we call an exact locally dense lattice. Closely related objects appear throughout the literature on computational lattice problems. Our constructions of lattices with large kissing number then follow as corollaries by showing that constructions due to Bennett and Peikert [RANDOM, 2023] (using Craig lattices) and Aggarwal and Stephens-Davidowitz [STOC, 2018] (using sparsification of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) in fact give exact locally dense lattices, as well as a new construction of exact locally dense lattices built from rotations of the $m$-dimensional checkerboard lattice $D_m$.
item.dc:creator: Huck Bennett, Minki Hhan, Zihan Li, Noah Stephens-Davidowitz

item.title: Survivor Set of Gauss Map with a Hole at $1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14534v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T$ be the Gauss map. For each $\alpha\in [0,1]$, let $E(\alpha)$ be the survivor set consisting of all $x\in [0,1]$ whose orbit $\{T^k(x):k\ge 0\}$ never enters the interval $(\alpha,1]$. We prove that the set-valued function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is increasing and locally constant almost everywhere. Moreover, we explicitly characterize all intervals where the function $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ remains constant. We also describe the points at which the map $\alpha\mapsto E(\alpha)$ is not locally constant. Further, we obtain the Hausdorff dimension of $E(\alpha)$ for all $\alpha\in [0,1]$. We prove that the function $\alpha\mapsto \dim_H(E(\alpha))$ forms a devil's staircase on $(0,1]$, but is not continuous at $0$. This discontinuity implies that the result of Raith [Acta Math. Univ. Comenian. 63 (1994), 39-53] fails for piecewise monotone interval maps with infinitely many branches. Finally, we give an application quantifying the set of points sharing identical $\alpha$-continued fraction expansion and regular continued fraction expansion.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Liu, Lingmin Liao

item.title: Overlap distributions under the Gibbs measure of a Haar model of $\log|\zeta|$ on and near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2610.14901v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Gibbs measure of $H(h) = \Re\sum_{p^{j} \leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(j p^{j(\sigma + i h)})$, a random field modeling large values of the log-modulus of the Riemann zeta function on and near the critical line, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. Writing $t = \log \log T$, the cutoff $X$ and real part $\sigma$ may vary with $T$ subject to $T^{1/t^{\Phi}} \leq X \leq T^{1/t^{\phi}}$ and $0 \leq \sigma - 1/2 \leq C_{\sigma}t^{\Phi}/\log T$, for fixed $\Phi \geq \phi > 1/2$ and $C_{\sigma} > 0$. On $I_{\theta} = [ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]$, define the Gibbs measure $G_{\beta,\sigma,T}^{\mathrm{H}}(\mathrm{d}h) := e^{\beta H(h)}\mathrm{d}h/\int_{I_{\theta}}e^{\beta H(h')}\mathrm{d}h'$. For every fixed $\theta > - 1$ and inverse temperature $\beta > 0$, the limiting joint distributions of correlations (overlaps) among points sampled from this measure are determined after averaging over the Haar phases. At and below $\beta_{c}(\theta) = 2\sqrt{1 + (\theta \vee 0)}$, the limiting two-overlap distribution is concentrated at $q_{0} = |\theta \wedge 0|$. Above this threshold, it assigns masses $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ and $1 - \beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$ to $q_{0}$ and $1$, respectively, and the limiting joint overlap distribution is described by a Poisson-Dirichlet process of parameter $\beta_{c}(\theta)/\beta$. Approximate Ghirlanda-Guerra identities are shown to hold uniformly for bounded deterministic functions of the sampled positions. This paper is the first in a series devoted to extending these results to $\log|\zeta|$ near the critical line.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: How iterated sumsets grow under the assumption of small doubling
item.description: arXiv:2610.15069v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K>1$ be a real number and let $A\subsetneq \mathbb Z$ be a finite and nonempty subset. Suppose $|A+A|<K|A|$. A fundamental open problem is to characterize the size of higher iterated sumsets $nA = A+\cdots+A$ ($n$-fold sumset). In 2004, Terry Tao formally posed the problem of determining the optimal growth function governing iterated sumsets of small-doubling sets. In this manuscript, we give a solution to this long-standing open problem for large enough $n$.
item.dc:creator: Dongchun Han, Qinghai Zhong

item.title: Polynomial Identities for Generalized Fibonacci Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.15131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Fibonacci, Lucas, and Pell sequences satisfy certain families of ``polynomial'' identities. While a few members of these families are well-known, we are not able to find a general statement of these identities in the mathematical literature. We show that such polynomial identities exist for many generalized Fibonacci sequences, and we classify sequences that have these identities obtained by two distinct approaches. One approach uses the Girard-Waring formula, while the other relies on Binet's formula and linear algebra.
item.dc:creator: Joey Glampe, Aryaman Joshi, Swagat Malla, Matthew Richey, Matthew Wright

item.title: A trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $\mathrm{GL}_{n}(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_{n}(E)$, with $E/F$ a quadratic extension of non-Archimedean local fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.15432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend the classical trace Paley-Wiener theorem for $p$-adic reductive groups, given by Bernstein, Deligne and Kazhdan in 1986, to a relative case. That is when $E/F$ is a quadratic extension of $p$-adic fields, the main result is a scalar Paley-Wiener theorem for relative Bessel distributions on $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\backslash \mathrm{GL}_n(E)$. These distributions are relative character of the form $$\pi\mapsto I_\pi (f), \ f\in C_c^\infty(\mathrm{GL}_n(E)),$$ as $\pi$ ranges over $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-distinguished irreducible tempered representations, and are constructed from a $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$-invariant functional and a Whittaker functional. Using the local Langlands correspondence, and the base-change from a unitary group, we show that the relative characters can be described as elements of the "generic" Bernstein center of the unitary group $U(n)$.
item.dc:creator: Juliette Coutens

item.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonn\'e theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the \'etale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.
item.dc:creator: Marco D'Addezio

item.title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
item.description: arXiv:2610.15648v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).
item.dc:creator: Patrick Ingram

item.title: Universal Shift Congruences for Weighted Permutation Sequences
item.description: arXiv:2610.15849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The involution numbers $1,1,2,4,10,26,\ldots$ repeat modulo $3$, $5$ and $7$. We explain this, and many similar patterns, by one rule. Many sequences count permutations in which every cycle of length $m$ carries a weight $w_m$ (involutions, derangements, "sets of lists", and many others in the OEIS). Writing $A(n)$ for such a count, the rule is $A(n+k)\equiv A(n)A(k)$ modulo $\mathrm{lcm}(n,k)$. It generalizes our earlier proof of the case modulo $k$ for one such sequence, but now it holds for all weights at once, as a coefficientwise congruence between universal polynomials, and we find the largest modulus that works for the universal polynomials, $nk/\mathrm{rad}(\gcd(n,k))$, and show that nothing larger does. We then show that passing from $k$ to $pk$ behaves like raising to the $p$-th power modulo a high power of $p$, with a sharp exponent for the polynomials, which gives $A(p^r)\equiv(w_1+(p-1)w_p)^{p^{r-1}}$ modulo $p^r$ for odd $p$, and explains why the prime $2$ is special. A family of sequences defined by Lagrange inversion fits the same framework, which proves Bala's conjecture for the whole family (the single sequence A278070 had been proved earlier by an automated system) and the divisibility observed in the entries A251568 and A251569. As further applications we prove OEIS conjectures of Richman, Hanna, van Hoeij and Bala (A227937), and the theorems apply to 101 OEIS sequences, whose congruences are recorded in a supplementary catalogue. Higher-order versions of the content formula are treated in a separate paper.
item.dc:creator: Ahaan Kallat

item.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
item.dc:creator: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Nonarchimedean discrete groups and quasi-isometric doubles of free groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.16291v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For any nonarchimedean local field $k$, we exhibit the first examples of Zariski-dense, discrete subgroups of special linear groups over $k$, which are not commensurable to any lattice in the points of a semisimple group over a local field, and contain an infinite index subgroup isomorphic to a lattice in the $k$-points of a higher rank $k$-semisimple group. We prove that any Gromov-hyperbolic double of a non-elementary free group along a cyclic subgroup embeds as a quasi-isometrically embedded subgroup of $\mathsf{SL}_5(k')\times \mathsf{SL}_5(k')$, where $k'$ is a discretely valued field. More precisely, $k'$ is the field of rational functions $k(t)$ equipped with the Gauss valuation and $k$ is any nonarchimedean local field of characteristic not equal to $2$ or $3$.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Tsouvalas

item.title: Depth-zero local Langlands via shtukas in mixed characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.16445v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assuming a smoothness property for mixed-characteristic shtuka spaces and hyperbolic localization for twisted sheaves, we determine the inertial restriction of the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter for irreducible depth-zero representations. Let $E$ be a non-archimedean local field of residue characteristic $p$, let $G$ be an unramified connected reductive group over $E$, and let $\pi$ be an irreducible smooth depth-zero representation of $G(E)$ over $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_{\ell}$ where $\ell$ is a prime number which does not divide $p|\pi_0Z(G)|$. Let $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ be the Fargues-Scholze $L$-parameter associated to $\pi$. We describe the restriction of $\varphi_{\pi}^{\operatorname{FS}}$ to the inertia subgroup in terms of Deligne-Lusztig theory. We prove this by computing the inertia action on the cohomology of shtuka spaces with depth-zero level structure. As an application, we prove that the Fargues--Scholze $L$-parameters agree with DeBacker--Reeder $L$-parameters over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\ell}$.
item.dc:creator: Chenji Fu

item.title: $2$-large sets are sets of nil-Bohr recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2610.16605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A set $S$ of positive integers is $2$-large if every two-coloring contains arbitrarily long monochromatic arithmetic progressions with common difference in $S$. We prove that every such set meets every nil-Bohr neighborhood of $0$. This proves a conjecture of the first author and gives a sharp answer to a question of Host, Kra, and Maass. We also show that, for every fixed nil-Bohr neighborhood \(B\) of \(0\) and every \(\eps>0\), restricting the common difference to \(B\) increases the extremal number for \(k\)-term arithmetic progressions by at most a factor of \(1+\eps\), provided \(k\) is sufficiently large.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Alweiss, Sohail Farhangi

item.title: Galois coinvariants and fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes
item.description: arXiv:2610.16760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Galois coinvariants of the geometric \'etale fundamental group and \'etale cohomology of varieties over a finitely generated field $k$. We establish finiteness properties of these coinvariants for (possibly infinite) Galois extensions $L/k$ such that $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ has finite exponent. As an application, we obtain a finiteness result for \'etale fundamental groups of arithmetic schemes over number fields.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Steklov

item.title: The weak cylinder conjecture for polynomial graphs of bounded degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.16803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ball's weak cylinder conjecture asserts that a set of $p^2$ points in $\mathrm{AG}(3,p)$ with at least $p$ non-determined directions is a union of $p$ parallel lines. We prove the conjecture for sets admitting a polynomial graph representation of total degree at most $D$, provided that $p>D^{9/2}$. More precisely, a non-cylindrical graph of degree $D\ge3$ satisfies $|\mathcal{N}_S|\le p+1-\lceil p/(D-1)\rceil$ under the same hypothesis. This bound is attained when $p\equiv1\pmod{D-1}$. The proof relates non-determined directions to permutation polynomials on parallel affine lines. A rigidity lemma for moving line restrictions, together with a reconstruction of their compositional components, bounds the number of contributing directions uniformly in $p$. Directions with affine restrictions are treated separately; all other contributions are bounded using geometric indecomposability and the Weil bound for plane curves.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bartoli, Alessandro Giannoni

item.title: Microlocal Arthur packets as a quasi-canonical basis of stable distributions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16931v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that microlocal Arthur packets can be reconstructed from an otherwise underdetermined system of linear equations arising from Kashiwara's local index theorem. The key is a geometric rigidity property of Arthur orbits which, together with Fourier symmetry, uniquely determines the microlocal multiplicities defining these packets. This realizes the associated Arthur distribution as the unique normalized element in the intersection of two filtered spaces of standard stable distributions related by Fourier transform. Under standard enhanced local Langlands hypotheses and Aubert compatibility, this gives an alternative representation-theoretic definition of microlocal Arthur packets for general connected reductive $p$-adic groups that does not use twisted endoscopy and ensures stability through the stability of tempered packet distributions. In the unipotent setting, we use this characterization to prove agreement between endoscopic and microlocal Arthur packets for split $\mathrm{SO}_{2n+1}$ when the residue characteristic is at least $6n+4$. We further use this characterization to compute all unipotent Arthur packets with unramified real infinitesimal character for inner-to-split adjoint exceptional $p$-adic groups. In this exceptional setting, we prove the microlocal weak Arthur packet conjecture and give counterexamples to the microlocal analogues of the least- and greatest-parameter conjectures.
item.dc:creator: Dan Ciubotaru, Emile Okada

item.title: Cyclotomic Structure and Exact Recurrences in Floquet Many-Body Quantum Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Periodically driven quantum systems exhibit a wide range of complex dynamics, including chaos. Yet, at special parameter values, their evolution can recur exactly. Several quantum protocols have recently been proposed that exploit exact Floquet recurrences to demonstrate genuine quantum advantage. Such recurrences can be studied through the arithmetic structure of the Floquet unitary. In this work, we establish a necessary and sufficient arithmetic criterion for exact recurrence and determine the minimal recurrence period when one exists. Because recurrence is a global property of the unitary, it holds for every initial state. Applying our framework requires only knowledge of the number field associated with the Hamiltonian parameters. We demonstrate the method using the kicked Ising chain, establishing exact recurrences in both Clifford and non-Clifford regimes. We further show that, in the recurrent non-Clifford regime, magic--a resource for quantum computation--is generated at intermediate times and undergoes exact periodic revivals enforced by the recurrence of the full Floquet unitary. By connecting number theory, quantum many-body dynamics, and quantum information, our work shows that exact recurrence extends beyond Clifford circuits and opens new avenues for magic generation and quantum hardware benchmarking.
item.dc:creator: Amit Anand, Dinesh Valluri, Shohini Ghose

item.title: p-adic Hodge theory of unipotent completions revisited
item.description: arXiv:2610.17169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension, and let $X/K$ be an algebraic variety. We present a new proof that the unipotent completion of the \'etale fundamental group of $X_{\bar{K}}$ is a pro-de Rham representation, and show that it is pro-semi-stable whenever $X$ has semi-stable \'etale cohomology. We also reprove, using syntomic methods, that it is pro-crystalline at integral base points whenever $X$ admits a smooth proper formal model. All three proofs use the bar construction and are inspired by Wojtkowiak's approach to unipotent fundamental groups.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Wild

item.title: Privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local systems are motivic
item.description: arXiv:2610.17173v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective variety over the complex numbers, and let $\mathbb{V}$ be an irreducible privileged $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system on $X$ in the sense of Esnault and Groechenig. We show that $\mathbb{V}$ is of geometric origin. We also give an example of a privileged but non-rigid $\mathrm{SL}_3$-local system.
item.dc:creator: Julia Meng, Charlie Wu

item.title: Square integrable representations and Hecke eigenvalues over a local non-archimedian field
item.description: arXiv:2610.17317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a split connected semi-simple group over a local non-archimedean field $F$. In this paper we study the action of Hecke operators on the Schwartz space of half-densities on the moduli stack $\bpo$ of $G$-bundles on ${\mathbb P}^1$ endowed with a trivialization at $0$ and $\infty$. This space is a representation of $G(F)\times G(F)$ which contains the regular representation of $G(F)$. We show that this inclusion is an isomorphism on the cuspidal part. In addition we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation $\pi$ of $G(F)$ defines a Hecke eigenvalue. As a byproduct we show that every irreducible square-integrable representation of $G(F)$ with an Iwahori fixed vector defines a ${\mathbb C}$-point on the Calogero-Moser space associated to $G$. We also show that for $G=PGL(N)$ the eigenvalues of certain "simplest non-trivial" Hecke operators are essentially equal to the values of the character of $\pi$ on regular elliptic elements. These results are parallel to some of the results of our previous publication where some analogous statements are proved in the case when $F$ is a finite field.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Braverman, David Kazhdan

item.title: Hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study hyperelliptic curves on $K3$ surfaces. We show that any number of general points on a $K3$ surface of Picard rank one can be connected by a hyperelliptic curve. As a by-product we recover the Beauville--Voisin decomposition of the small diagonal, together with some new bounds on its torsion order in the integral Chow group. On the arithmetic side, given a $K3$ surface $X$ of geometric Picard rank one defined over a number field $k$, we show that there exists a finite extension $k\subset k'$ such that quadratic points are dense in $X_{k'}$, extending a theorem of Corvaja--Zucconi to $K3$ surfaces of arbitrary degree.
item.dc:creator: Federico Moretti

item.title: Moduli descriptions of v-sheaf local models
item.description: arXiv:2610.17878v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a uniform moduli-theoretic description of the v-sheaf local model $\mathbb{M}_{\mathcal G,\mu}$ for an arbitrary parahoric group scheme $\mathcal G$ and an arbitrary dominant cocharacter $\mu$. Our approach is Tannakian and builds on a new theory of parahoric induced modules. When $\mu$ is minuscule, this framework explains the linear-algebraic conditions arising in the theory of local models of Shimura varieties.
item.dc:creator: Jo\~ao Louren\c{c}o, Timo Richarz, Eva Viehmann, Torsten Wedhorn

item.title: Integral trace duality and the Witt filtration on Lubin--Tate space
item.description: arXiv:2610.18246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal O$ be the Lubin--Tate deformation ring of a one-dimensional commutative formal group of finite height $n\geq1$ over a perfect field $k$ of characteristic $p$. We identify Rezk's Witt filtration $\{I_d\}$ with the divisibility filtration of integral trace pairings on subgroup algebras of fixed source lifts. This gives the geometric recursion \[ I_{d+1}=pI_d+J_{d,z}\qquad(d\geq0), \] where $J_{d,z}$ defines the targets of order-$p^d$ quotient isogenies from a $W(k)$-valued lift $z$ of the closed point. The corrected ideal is independent of $z$. We also compute the cokernel of the universal source trace pairing over $\mathcal O$: it is $\bigoplus_{j=1}^d(\mathcal O/p^j)^{r_j-r_{j-1}}$, where $r_j$ counts order-$p^j$ subgroups of $(\mathbf Q_p/\mathbf Z_p)^n$. The same duality extends the generic trace along two-step isogeny flags to an integral surjection, even when the flag-forgetting map is not flat. This computes composition in the subring of weighted trace operations. Applications include sharp projector denominators and congruence fibre products for full-torsion loci.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Taccani

item.title: Proof of a nonnegativity conjecture of Prellberg--Stanton
item.description: arXiv:2610.18377v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 1994, Friedman, Joichi and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $q+(1-q)\prod_{i=n}^{2n-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i}}$ are nonnegative for $n\geq3$ and $n$ being odd. Let $\qbinom nm$ denote the Gaussian polynomial. In 2003, Prellberg and Stanton conjectured that coefficients of the power-series $(1-q)\qbinom nm\prod_{i=0}^{m-1}\frac{1}{1-q^{i+m}}$ are nonnegative for $0<m<n$, except when $n$ is even and $m\in\{2,n-2\}$. The latter conjecture implies the former. In this paper, we prove a stronger result concerning coefficientwise nonnegativity of another power series, which implies the conjecture of Prellberg and Stanton. The proof uses a M\"obius correction from Gaussian polynomials, weight-preserving injections on partitions, explicit linearly independent vectors in the kernel of a derivation operator and the KOH identity.
item.dc:creator: Hong-Zhang Ai, Lili Mu, Bao-Xuan Zhu

item.title: Multidimensional Szemer\'edi Theorem for Pairwise Independent Jointly Intersective Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.18657v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a new approach to the Joint Intersectivity Conjecture of Bergelson, Leibman, and Lesigne for commuting transformations. The conjecture asserts that the necessary divisibility condition is the only obstruction to polynomial multiple recurrence and, consequently, to the multidimensional polynomial Szemer\'edi theorem. We establish the conjecture for pairwise independent polynomials, obtaining the first general result for sequences of arbitrary length beyond the classical one-transformation setting. Our argument is inspired by the Furstenberg-Katznelson approach and its polynomial enhancement due to Bergelson-Leibman. Its main novelty, however, lies in the development of new techniques that allow us to bypass the use of the polynomial van der Waerden theorem, on which these methods traditionally rely, and for which no suitable analogue is currently available in our setting. In particular, we prove a Nil-Bohr returns theorem for compact extensions in systems with nilpotent structure, as well as a nil-plus-null decomposition for polynomial multicorrelation sequences that preserves joint intersectivity and positivity.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Davide Sclosa

item.title: Proofs of four Takigiku--Tsuchioka conjectures on level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18666v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove four conjectures of Takigiku and Tsuchioka consisting of eight Rogers--Ramanujan type identities. Two conjectures involve triple sums and a third involves quadruple sums, and their product sides are certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{13}^{(2)}$. The fourth conjecture gives multisum representations of certain level $2$ principal characters of $A_{2\ell-1}^{(2)}$. The proofs rely on the Bailey pair method, finite sum identities involving Gaussian polynomials, and the quintuple product identity.
item.dc:creator: Liuquan Wang

item.title: T-modules and Pila-Wilkie estimates
item.description: arXiv:1311.5617v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $T-$modules, introduced by G. Anderson in the '80s, are the natural analogue of abelian varieties in Function Field Arithmetic in positive characteristic. For a special class of them we highlight that a totally similar description of the classic Weierstrass function still holds. In particular, torsion points correspond modulo a finite-rank lattice to rational points of the tangent space. We present in this work an upper bound estimate of the number of rational points of the trascendent part of the analytic set corresponding, into the tangent space, to a nontrivial algebraic subvariety of a $T-$module of this special class. Such an estimate, which takes the same shape of that proved by J. Pila and J. Wilkie, represents our first step of our strategy to prove Manin-Mumford conjecture for such special $T-$modules, based on the ideas developped by U. Zannier and J. Pila.
item.dc:creator: Luca Demangos

item.title: Level one automorphic representations of an anisotropic exceptional group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$
item.description: arXiv:2407.05859v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Up to isomorphism, there is a unique connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of Lie type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be such a group. In this paper, we study the level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ in the spirit of the work of Chenevier, Renard, and Ta\"ibi. First, we give an explicit formula for the number of these representations having any given archimedean component. For this, we study the automorphism group of the two definite exceptional Jordan algebras of rank $27$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ studied by Gross, as well as the dimension of the invariants of these groups in all irreducible representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$. Then, assuming standard conjectures by Arthur and Langlands for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, we refine this counting by studying the contribution of the representations whose global Arthur parameter has any possible image (or "Sato-Tate group"). This includes a detailed description of all those images, as well as precise statements for the Arthur's multiplicity formula in each case. As a consequence, we obtain a conjectural but explicit formula for the number of algebraic, cuspidal, level one automorphic representation of $\mathrm{GL}_{26}$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ with Sato-Tate group $\mathbf{F}_{4}(\mathbb{R})$ of any given weight (assumed "$\mathrm{F}_{4}$-regular"). The first example of such representations occurs in motivic weight $36$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Shan

item.title: On a determinant involving linear combinations of Legendre symbols
item.description: arXiv:2408.07034v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a conjecture of the second author by evaluating the determinant $$\det\left[x + \left(\frac{i-j}p\right) + \left(\frac ip\right)y + \left(\frac jp\right)z + \left(\frac{ij}p\right)w\right]_{0\le i,j\le(p-3)/2}$$ for any odd prime $p$, where $(\frac{\cdot}p)$ denotes the Legendre symbol. In particular, the determinant is equal to $x$ when $p\equiv 3\pmod4$.
item.dc:creator: Keqin Liu, Zhi-Wei Sun, Li-Yuan Wang

item.title: On sparsity of integral points in orbits and correspondences with big iterated pullbacks
item.description: arXiv:2501.04642v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove new unconditional results of sparsity of integral points on orbits under many maps and correspondences in arbitrary dimensions, generalizing theorems of Yasufuku(2015) and others. The main ingredients are new diophantine approximation tools and recent constructions for correspondences due to Ingram (2011).
item.dc:creator: Jorge Mello

item.title: The global exceptional theta correspondence for the dual pair $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times \mathbf{PGL}_{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2501.19101v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ be the unique (up to isomorphism) connected semisimple algebraic group over $\mathbb{Q}$ of type $\mathrm{F}_{4}$, with compact real points and split over $\mathbb{Q}_{p}$ for all primes $p$. A conjectural computation by the author in arxiv:2407.05859 predicts the existence of a family of level one automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$, which are expected to be functorial lifts of cuspidal representations of $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with Hecke eigenforms. In this paper, we study the exceptional theta correspondence for $\mathbf{F}_{4}\times\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, and establish the existence of such a family of automorphic representations for $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. Moreover, we show that for the automorphic form on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$ associated with any even weight $k\geq 12$, level $N$ cuspidal eigenform, its global theta lift to $\mathbf{F}_{4}$ is non-zero. For the other direction, motivated by the work of Pollack, we develop a notion of "exceptional theta series" on $\mathbf{PGL}_{2}$, arising from certain automorphic representations of $\mathbf{F}_{4}$. These theta series are holomorphic modular forms on $\mathbf{SL}_{2}(\mathbb{Z})$, with explicit Fourier expansions, and span the entire space of level one cusp forms.
item.dc:creator: Yi Shan

item.title: Root numbers for twisted Fermat quotient curves
item.description: arXiv:2503.22991v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\ell$ be an odd prime, $N \geq 1$ be an integer, and $\delta \geq 1$ be a $\ell^N$-th power free integer such that ${\rm ord}_{\ell}(\delta) = 0$ or $\ell \nmid {\rm ord}_{\ell}(\delta)$. In this paper, we give an explicit formula for the root number of the Hecke character associated with a certain quotient curve of the twisted Fermat curve $X^{\ell^N} + Y^{\ell^N} = \delta$. This result gives a generalization of Stoll (2002) and Shu (2021).
item.dc:creator: Ryosuke Yanagihara

item.title: Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line and multiplicative chaos
item.description: arXiv:2506.16115v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we prove that the Dirichlet $L$-functions $L(1/2+ix,\chi_q)$, where $\chi_q$ is a uniformly random Dirichlet character modulo $q$ and $x\in \mathbb{R}$, converge as $q\to \infty$ to a random Schwartz distribution $\zeta_{\mathrm{rand}}$, which is related to complex Gaussian multiplicative chaos (GMC). This is the same limiting object that appeared in \cite{SaWe20a}, where the authors proved that the random shifts of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line $\zeta(1/2+ix+i\omega T)$, where $\omega\sim \mathrm{Unif} ([0,1])$, converge as $T\to \infty$. As an application of our method, we also prove that to the right of the critical line, that is, for $\Re(s)>1/2$, the convergence of the random $L$-functions $L(s,\chi_q)$ occurs in the space of analytic functions, if we exclude the zero probability (in the limit $q\to \infty$) event that $\chi_q$ is the principal character. This was already proven in \cite{Ba81a}, but our method provides a novel proof of this fact. Our results hold for moduli $q=q_n$ such that the smallest prime divisor of $q_n$ tends to $\infty$ as $n\to\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Sami Vihko

item.title: Truncated Hypergeometric Functions and Discretized Integrals
item.description: arXiv:2507.19793v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a kind of finite truncation of the hypergeometric series and provide its discretized integral representation. This is motivated by recent results of Maesaka-Seki-Watanabe and Hirose-Matsusaka-Seki on the identity between truncated series and discretized integrals which comes from the mutliple zeta values and multiple polylogarithms. We also prove the formula of Ohno-Zagier type which relates the truncated multiple polylogarithms and the truncated hypergeometric series.
item.dc:creator: Shuji Yamamoto

item.title: A central limit theorem for partitions involving generalised divisor functions
item.description: arXiv:2510.19740v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We let $p_f(n,k)$ count the $f$-restricted coloured partitions of $n$ with $k$ parts, for a positive integer valued function $f$, given by the bivariate generating series \[ Q_f(z,u) := 1+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} p_f(n,k) u^kz^n =\prod_{k=1}^{\infty}(1+uz^k)^{\Delta_f(k)}, \] where $\Delta_f(n)=|f(n+1)-f(n)|$. A part of size $n$ has $\Delta_f(n)$ distinguishable colours, and each coloured part is available at most once. In this article, we establish a central limit theorem for the number of summands in such partitions when $f(n)=\sigma_r(n)$ denotes the generalised divisor function, defined as $\sigma_r(n)=\sum_{d|n}d^r$ for integer $r\geq 2$. This problem is related to the work of Lipnik, Madritsch, and Tichy on restricted partitions into the indexed values $\lfloor m^{\alpha}\rfloor$, with $0<\alpha<1$. A key element of our proof relies on the analytic behaviour of the Dirichlet series \begin{align*} \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{|\sigma_r(n+1)-\sigma_r(n)|}{n^s}, \end{align*} for $\mathrm{Re}(s)>r+1$. We study this problem employing the identity involving the Ramanujan sum. Furthermore, we analyse the Euler product arising in this analysis by adopting the argument of Alkan, Ledoan and Zaharescu. The absolute values are handled using an eventual parity pattern, and the required continuation is obtained from the corrected character decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Madhuparna Das, Nicolas Robles

item.title: Estimating the number of zeros of Dedekind zeta-functions
item.description: arXiv:2510.27444v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, I develop a new approach to estimating the number of non-trivial zeros of a Dedekind zeta function with absolute height at most $T\ge1$, counted with multiplicity. The method yields an explicit zero-counting estimate with constants $(C_1,C_2,C_3)=(0.194,7.806,1.808)$. For the Riemann zeta function, it gives the error bound $0.097\log T+4.807$.
item.dc:creator: Victor Amberger

item.title: Second moments of general Dirichlet series and Selberg zeta functions at $\sigma = 1$
item.description: arXiv:2511.07100v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove the existence of the second moment at $\sigma=1$ for a general Dirichlet series with positive coefficients whose partial sum of the coefficients up to $x$ satisfies $\varrho x+O(x/(\log x)^{1+\varepsilon})$ for some $\varepsilon>0$. The result extends a theorem of Broucke and Hilberdink. As applications, we establish the existence of the second moment for Beurling zeta functions satisfying a prime number theorem with a power-saving error term and for the Selberg zeta function for every cofinite Fuchsian group.
item.dc:creator: Ram\=unas Garunk\v{s}tis, Jok\=ubas Putrius

item.title: Sporadic points on $X_0(N)$
item.description: arXiv:2511.09015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine all integers $N$ for which the modular curve $X_0(N)$ admits a sporadic CM point (of any degree), as well as all $N$ for which $X_0(N)$ admits a sporadic point, whether CM or non-CM. In a sense, our results generalize the classification of isogenies of elliptic curves over $\Q$ due to Mazur and Kenku: their work determines the $X_0(N)$ with degree 1 sporadic points, whereas we classify all $X_0(N)$ that have a sporadic point of arbitrary degree.
item.dc:creator: Maarten Derickx, Filip Najman

item.title: Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework
item.description: arXiv:2511.13879v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present an algorithm for studying the sum $$ G_N(x,\rho) = \sum_{k=1}^N \left[ \{x+k\rho\} - \frac{1}{2}\right],$$ which is closely related to the discrepancy of the irrational rotation. Computation of $ G_N $ and associated statistics is notoriously difficult due to numerical instability and the failure of sampling to capture the discontinuities. Our algorithm instead fully defines $G_N$ through its discontinuities, which allows computation of $ G_N (x,\rho)$ with errors on the order of $N$ times machine epsilon in $O(N)$ time for practical $N$. The associated probability density function can then be computed in $O(N \log N)$ time. Presented as a tool for experimental mathematics, the algorithm enables reliable plots of the descriptive statistics of $G_N$ over $N$, in particular the length of the support of the $\text{pdf}$ (the discrepancy), revealing extremal behavior related to the arithmetic properties of $\rho$. We also observe a new pattern: when $\rho$ is well approximated by a continued-fraction convergent $\frac{p_n}{q_n}$, the $\text{pdf}$ exhibits a predictable spiked-trapezoidal pattern when $N=kq_n$, eventually degrading at a rate that appears to depend on approximation quality.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Kravitz, H. (2026). Computational Study of Irrational Rotations via Exact Discontinuity Tracking: A New Experimental Framework. Experimental Mathematics
item.dc:creator: Hannah Kravitz

item.title: Finite fields whose members are the sum of a potent and a 5-potent
item.description: arXiv:2512.16942v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that there are only finitely many finite fields whose members are the sum of an $n$-potent element and a $5$-potent element. Combining this with the algorithmic results provided by S.D. Cohen {\it et al.}, we confirm in the affirmative the conjecture posed in \cite{Cohen} concerning all finite fields satisfying this condition. Furthermore, we obtain several elementary results related to the more general problem of decomposing every element of a finite field into the sum of an $m$-potent and an $n$-potent (as formulated in \cite{Cohen}), proving that the number of finite fields satisfying this condition is finite.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Zhou, Peter V. Danchev, Hongfeng Wu

item.title: Lattice coverings and homogeneous covering congruences
item.description: arXiv:2601.03212v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of covering $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with a finite number of sublattices of finite index; this may be viewed as a projective, or homogeneous, version of the well-known problem of covering systems of congruences. We give a construction of minimal coverings which produces many, but not all, minimal coverings, prove an inequality relating the size of a covering to the least common multiple of the lattice indices, and determine all minimal coverings with at most $8$ sublattices.
item.dc:creator: J. E. Cremona, P. Koymans

item.title: Improving bounds for value sets of polynomials over finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2601.03548v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_{q}$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$, and let $f \in \mathbb{F}_{q}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree $d > 0$. Denote the image set of this polynomial as $V_{f}=\{f(\alpha)\mid\alpha\in\mathbb{F}_{q}\}$ and denote the cardinality of this set as $N_{f}$. A much sharper bound for $N_{f}$ is established in this paper. In particular, for any $p\neq 2, 3$, and for nearly every generic quartic polynomial $f \in \mathbb{F}_{q}[x]$, we obtain $$\lvert N_f - \frac{5}{8} q \rvert \leq \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{q} + \frac{33}{8},$$ which holds as a simple corollary of the main result.
item.dc:creator: Jiyou Li, Zhiyao Zhang

item.title: BSD Invariants and Murmurations of Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2603.04604v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the murmurations of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ depend on the invariants in the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer formula, using the Frobenius traces at all primes up to $10^5$ for one curve in each isogeny class of conductor below $10^5$. In these data, at the murmuration scale the rank-$0$ profile depends on the central value $L(E,1)$, in its shape and in the position of its sign changes. Through the series for $L(E,1)$, the covariance of $a_p$ with $L(E,1)$ is exactly a sum of covariances of $a_p$ with the coefficients $a_n$ weighted by a factor that depends on $n$ and the conductor; numerically, in this conductor range, the terms with $n\le50$ reproduce its shape (correlation $0.998$, largest deviation $0.29$ against a largest absolute covariance of $3.03$). Empirically, for $q=3$, $5$, $7$ and $11$ the unweighted covariance of $a_p$ with $a_q$ has nearly the shape of the rank-$0$ profile dilated by a factor near $q$; for $q=2$ the agreement is weaker. Weighting by the Tamagawa product changes the rank-$0$ profile substantially on $0.025<y\le0.125$; after standardisation to the deciles of $\log L(E,1)$, the change summed over these bins is 13% of the unstandardised one (17% for sums of absolute values), and in the lowest bin the standardised change is larger than the unstandardised one and of opposite sign. This version replaces the earlier versions (v1 and v2); their claim that the Tate-Shafarevich group carries information about Frobenius traces beyond the other invariants taken together cannot hold, because its analytic order is defined by the BSD formula, and it is withdrawn.
item.dc:creator: Dane Wachs

item.title: Murmurations, Periods, and Local Factors
item.description: arXiv:2603.22807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note replaces arXiv:2603.22807v1 and withdraws its three theorems, which do not stand as stated. Theorem A, that the order of the Tate-Shafarevich group of $y^2=x^3+x+D(t)$ over $\mathbb{F}_q(t)$ is determined by the cyclotomic type of the $L$-polynomial, holds at rank $0$ when $D$ has degree $5$ but fails at positive rank; we give a counterexample and cite the correct statement. Theorem B is Tur\'an's inequality for modified Bessel functions; we prove a version for general even weights and a class of increasing tilts that includes the Euler factor, which gives the Euler-factor tilt at every prime. Theorem C, a limit law for the covariance of $a_p$ with the real period at fixed $L(f,1)$, was not proved, and we explain why. We also recompute the empirical section of the first version from Cremona's tables, correct its numbers, withdraw those we could not reconstruct, and show that its sign flip at $p=3$ and its "100% Tamagawa channel" are artefacts of decile conditioning and of the rank-$0$ BSD formula.
item.dc:creator: Dane Wachs

item.title: There are infinitely many Hilbert cubes of dimension 3 in the set of squares
item.description: arXiv:2604.05459v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an integer tuple $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ with $a_i\neq0$ for $i=1,\ldots,d$, we define the associated Hilbert cube by \[ H(a_0;a_1,\ldots,a_d) = \left\{ a_0+\sum_{i=1}^d \varepsilon_i a_i: \varepsilon_i\in\{0,1\} \right\}. \] We call $(a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_d)$ a $d$-dimensional Hilbert-cube presentation. We prove that there are $\gg N^{1/4}$ reduced Hilbert-cube presentations $(a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3)$ with $a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3\in[0,N]$ such that \[ H(a_0;a_1,a_2,a_3)\subset \mathcal{S}, \] where $\mathcal{S}=\{m^2:\;m\in\Z\}$. Moreover, we prove that for each $i, j\in\{0, 1, 2, 3\}$ with $i<j$, the set $$ \left\{\frac{a_{i}}{a_{j}}:\;H(a_{0}; a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3})\subset \cal{S} \;\text{and}\;a_{i}>0\;\text{for}\;i=0, 1, 2, 3\;\right\} $$ is dense in the set of positive real numbers (in the Euclidean topology).
item.dc:creator: Andrew Bremner, Christian Elsholtz, Maciej Ulas

item.title: On the Number of Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers
item.description: arXiv:2604.15042v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that there are infinitely many $n$ such that $\omega(n+k) \ll \log k$ for all integers $k \ge 2$. This improves on a result of Tao and Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen (2025), who have $O(k)$ in place of $O(\log k)$. As corollaries, we make progress on a number of questions posed by Erd\H{o}s. The proof is based on a quantitative refinement of the Tao-Ter\"{a}v\"{a}inen probabilistic argument, combining a refined sieve construction with upper bounds for high moments and the resulting tail estimates. Moreover, we formulate a conjecture on integers with many prime factors based on Cram\'{e}r-type random models. Assuming this conjecture, the main bound is essentially sharp.
item.dc:creator: Cheuk Fung Lau

item.title: The sum-product phenomenon for dense subsets of finite fields
item.description: arXiv:2604.17117v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be a finite field of prime order $p$ and let $A \subset \mathbb{F}_p$ be a subset. In the dense regime when $|A| \geq \alpha p$ for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$, we determine the optimal constant $f(\alpha)$ in the inequality $$ \max(|A+A|, |A\cdot A|) \geq (f(\alpha) - o(1))p. $$ The proof relies on a structural result for sumsets of dense subsets, established via a regularity lemma in general finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Xuancheng Shao

item.title: Reductions of $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Q_{p^f})$-Banach spaces of slopes in $(0,1)$
item.description: arXiv:2605.02654v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $f \geq 1$. We consider a $p$-adic locally algebraic $\text{GL}_2(\mathbb Q_{p^f})$-representation attached to a tuple of $f$ weights $k=(k_i)$ for $0 \leq i \leq f-1$ and a $p$-adic integer $a_p$ with valuation in $(0,1)$. We give conditions under which the irreducible quotients of the subquotients in a filtration on the reduction mod $p$ of the natural integral structure on this space are supercuspidal. We also check that for small $k$ and $f$ the integral structure is a lattice so that the mod $p$ reduction is nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Eknath Ghate, Shivansh Pandey

item.title: Hecke Eigenvalues of Ikeda Lifts
item.description: arXiv:2605.16083v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the Hecke eigenvalues of Ikeda lifts. Using the spherical map for the Hecke algebra of the symplectic group, we obtain an explicit formula for the eigenvalues $\lambda_F(p^r)$. From this formula, we show that $\lambda_F(p^r)$ can be written as a polynomial in $p^{\pm 1/2}$ with a positive leading term. Furthermore, we prove that the coefficients of this polynomial are bounded and, as a consequence, the Hecke eigenvalues $\lambda_F(p^r)$ are positive for all sufficiently large primes $p$.
item.dc:creator: Nagarjuna Chary Addanki, Ameya Pitale

item.title: On modular forms of rational weight satisfying the canonical second-order linear modular differential equation
item.description: arXiv:2605.23383v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we completely classify the rational weights $k$ for which the Kaneko-Zagier (KZ) differential equation admits a fundamental system of solutions consisting of modular forms for a principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(N)$. By transforming the KZ equation into a hypergeometric differential equation, we study the global analytic continuation of its solutions, adopting an approach analogous to Stiller's work on Picard-Fuchs equations. We explicitly construct the monodromy representation matrices corresponding to the elements of the principal congruence subgroups and completely determine the algebraic conditions under which these connection matrices commute. Leveraging these stringent commutativity constraints, we prove that the weights $k$ yielding modular solutions are strictly limited to $k \equiv 1/2, 7/2, 1, 2, 3 \pmod{6}$ and $k = (6n+1)/5$, thereby demonstrating that no modular solutions exist beyond those previously discovered by Kaneko and Koike. Furthermore, the commutative algebras generated by these connection matrices reveal a profound analogy with commuting transfer matrices in quantum integrable systems.
item.dc:creator: Yuichi Sakai, Hiroyuki Tsutsumi

item.title: Counting the number of $1_{m}$-preperiodic $\mathcal{O}_{K}$-points of a discrete dynamical system with applications from arithmetic statistics, VII
item.description: arXiv:2606.14468v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this follow-up article of a multi-part series on (strictly) preperiodic point-counting, we inspect an astonishing relationship between the set of (strictly) $1_{m}$-preperiodic points of a polynomial map $\varphi_{d, c}$ defined by $\varphi_{d, c}(z) = z^d + c$ for all $c, z \in \mathcal{O}_{K}$ and the coefficient $c$, where $K$ is any number field of degree $n\geq 1$, $d>2$ is an integer and $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ is any fixed (eventual period). As before, we study counting problems that are inspired by torsion point-counting in arithmetic statistics and (strictly) preperiodic point-counting in arithmetic dynamics. In doing so, we then first prove that for any prime $p\geq 3$ and for any fixed $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and fixed (eventual period) $m\in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{p^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Inspired further by work of Doyle-Poonen along with conjectural work of Hutz and $\textit{abc}(\textit{d})$-conditional work of Panraksa on $K$-rational preperiodic points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ for any prime $p\geq 5$ in arithmetic dynamics, we then also prove that for any fixed (eventual period) $m \in \mathbb{Z}_{ \geq 1}$, the average number of distinct $1_{m}$-preperiodic integral points of any $\varphi_{(p-1)^{\ell}, c}$ modulo prime $p\mathcal{O}_{K}$ is unbounded or zero as $c\to \infty$. Finally, we then apply counting and distribution results from arithmetic statistics, and then get counting and statistical results on arithmetic objects arising naturally in our polynomial discrete dynamical settings. Together with the previous articles in the series, it might then be fair to view this article as an attempt to contribute to "arithmetic statistical dynamics".
item.dc:creator: Brian Kintu

item.title: On concatenations of two $k$-generalized Pell numbers
item.description: arXiv:2606.15290v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the concatenation of two $k$-generalized Pell numbers. More precisely, we determine all solutions of the equation $P_n^{(k)} = P_m^{(k)} \cdot 10^{d} + P_p^{(k)}$, where $d$ is the number of decimal digits of $P_p^{(k)}$. We prove that for $k \ge 3$ there are no solutions, while for $k = 2$ the only solution is $P_4 = 12 = 1\|2$.
item.dc:creator: Cherif B. Deme, Kancou D. Fall, Khady Faye, Bernadette Faye

item.title: Harder's conjecture and Hermitian automorphic forms
item.description: arXiv:2606.30063v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k\ge4$ and $j\ge2$ be integers with $j$ even. Harder's conjecture predicts a congruence between a primitive elliptic cusp form of weight $2k+j-2$ and a degree-two vector-valued Siegel Hecke cusp eigenform of weight ${\det}^{k}\mathrm{Sym}^{j}$. We prove the corresponding Harder-type congruence for the spinor $L$-polynomials under explicit arithmetic hypotheses on a congruence prime and an auxiliary imaginary quadratic field. Our approach uses Hermitian automorphic forms on the quasi-split unitary group $\mathrm{U}_{2,2}$. We construct Hermitian spin lifts of Siegel cusp forms and show that the Hermitian cusp form produced by a Hermitian Klingen-Eisenstein congruence lies in the image of this lift. The key step is to prove that the Galois representation attached to this Hermitian cusp form is conjugate invariant. For this, we combine the endoscopic classification for quasi-split unitary groups with Selmer-group vanishing results. This allows us to identify the Hermitian cusp form as the spin lift of a Siegel cusp eigenform and thereby obtain the Harder-type congruence. The argument applies uniformly to both even and odd $k$.
item.dc:creator: Hidenori Katsurada, Nobuki Takeda

item.title: An incremental approximation to the prime-counting function via polygonal numbers
item.description: arXiv:2606.31761v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct an incremental prime-counting approximation from corrected right-endpoint sums on polygonal-number partitions. For each fixed polygonal family, retaining completed contributions gives $\mathcal O(1)$ numerical operations per consecutive node and $\mathcal O(\sqrt X)$ operations for the full traversal through $X$, in the unit-cost model. The scheme uses a fixed number of working numerical words rather than repeated summation. Asymptotic formulas for the discretization error and terminal scale yield an unconditional relation with the classical normalized prime-counting error. We prove that the logarithmic mean of the normalized estimator error converges to $1/\sqrt2$ if and only if the Riemann hypothesis holds, and give an independent Mellin proof of the converse. Under the hypothesis, this constant uniquely removes the limiting signed mean bias. Computations at powers of ten through $10^{19}$ with coefficient $0.7071$ show accuracy comparable to the Riemann approximation at the sampled arguments
item.dc:creator: Artur Samojluk, Artur Siemaszko

item.title: Sign Patterns in a Two Colored Partition Companion series
item.description: arXiv:2607.10576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study three closely related questions arising from the recent work of Andrews and El Bachraoui on the two-color partition series \[ S_1(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}s_1(n)q^n=\sum_{a\ge0}q^a(-q^{a+1};q)_\infty^2 \] and its odd companion, denoted by $T_o(q)$. First, for the eta-normalized companion \[ C(q)=(q;q)_\infty T_o(q)=\sum_{n\ge0}c(n)q^n, \] we prove a strong form of the Andrews--El Bachraoui sign conjecture that $\limsup c(n)=+\infty$ and $\liminf c(n)=-\infty$. Second, we construct an involution using the Franklin-type involution of Chen and Liu to combinatorially explain Andrews--El Bachraoui congruence for $s_1(n)$ modulo 4. Third, we introduce a two-variable refinement of $S_1(q)$ which records the difference of the lengths of the two colored components. Using Ramanujan's partial theta identity and heat-type equations, we obtain a closed formula for all of its even moments, and we show that the eta-normalized moments satisfy termwise congruences modulo $p^{2k}$ for every prime $p\equiv5\pmod6$.
item.dc:creator: Aritram Dhar, Ankush Goswami, Mohit Tripathi

item.title: The First Moment of Dirichlet L-functions over Generators of the Character Group
item.description: arXiv:2607.14612v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We evaluate the average of the central values $L(1/2,\chi)$ over the generators of the group of Dirichlet characters modulo $q$, as $q\to\infty$ through the primes.
item.dc:creator: Rizwanur Khan

item.title: Orthogonality Defects of HKZ-Reduced Bases
item.description: arXiv:2608.22943v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $D_n$ denote the supremum of the orthogonality defects over all $n$-dimensional Hermite--Korkine--Zolotarev (HKZ)-reduced bases. This paper shows that, as $n\to\infty$, \[ \log D_n=2n\log n-n\log\log n+O(n). \] We also determine the exact value $D_4=4375/1024$.
item.dc:creator: Zhixing Li

item.title: Fourier Coefficients of the Degenerate Eisenstein Series on Symplectic Groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.24719v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study degenerate Eisenstein series on symplectic groups and construct a new automorphic descent. We show that a certain Fourier coefficient, after restriction to a smaller symplectic group, is itself an Eisenstein series with the same inducing parameter \(s\). We describe the resulting holomorphic section explicitly in terms of the original section and local \(L\)-factors at unramified places. At every regular point of the local descent, we prove surjectivity at non-Archimedean places and dense image at Archimedean places. We finally indicate an application of the iterated descent to maximal Fourier coefficients of Eisenstein series.
item.dc:creator: Alan Xuelun Hou, Yusheng Lei

item.title: On lifting representations and actions on curves of the metacyclic groups $C_{p^s}\rtimes C_m$
item.description: arXiv:2609.03191v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a prime $p$, a pair $(s,m)\in\mathbb{N}^2$ with $m$ relatively prime to $p$, a homomorphism $\chi:C_m\rightarrow\operatorname{Aut}(C_{p^s})$, and an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p$, we consider the semidirect product $G=C_{p^s}\rtimes_{\chi} C_m$, the $p$-Sylow subgroup $H\cong C_{p^s}$ of $G$, and a $k[G]$-module $V$. Let $R$ be a complete discrete valuation ring of residue field $k$ and mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ that contains a primitive $p^s$-th root of unity. If $\chi$ is injective, we present two necessary and sufficient criteria for lifting $V$ to an $R[G]$-module $\widetilde{V}$ which is a free $R$-module: (i) when no extra requirement is made on $\widetilde{V}$ and (ii) when we require $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. The criteria correct several results in the literature and we use them to prove that, if $\chi$ is injective and $G$ acts faithfully on a connected smooth projective curve $X$ over $k$, then, under mild hypotheses satisfied if $X\rightarrow X/G$ is a Harbater--Katz--Gabber cover, the $k[G]$-module $H^0(X,\Omega_X)$ has a lift $\widetilde{V}$ to $R$ with $\widetilde{V}^H=\{0\}$. Also, with $B:=R[\frac{1}{p}]$, we prove the following obstruction when $p$ is odd, $m$ is even, $\chi$ is injective, and $X/C_{p^s}\cong\mathbb{P}^1_k$: if no such lift $\widetilde{V}$ exists with the $B[H]$-module $\widetilde{V}\otimes_R B$ defined over $\mathbb{Q}$, then the action of $G$ on $X$ does not lift to $R$.
item.dc:creator: Huy Dang, Adrian Vasiu

item.title: Cyclotomy of symmetric polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2609.09232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove some new identities for homogeneous symmetric polynomials when evaluated at roots of unity. Some of these formulas are applied to obtain new insights onto cyclotomic polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Laura De Carli, Maurizio Laporta

item.title: On the Number of Hecke Eigenvalues of the Same Sign on $\mathrm{GL}_n$
item.description: arXiv:2609.10446v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the distribution of signs of the (real-valued) Hecke eigenvalues $A(m,1,...,1)$ of self-dual Hecke--Maass cusp forms for the group $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb Z)$, where $n\geq 2$ is an integer. Our main result establishes, under the Generalised Ramanujan--Petersson Conjecture, that for all $X\leq x\leq 2X$ outside a set of measure $o(X)$ the short interval $(x,x+H]$ contains at least $H(\log X)^{1/n^2-1}$ indices with both positive and negative Hecke eigenvalues, provided that $(\log X)^{1-1/n^2+\varepsilon}\leq H\leq X/10$. For $\mathrm{GL}_2$ Hecke--Maass cusp forms we obtain a stronger bound unconditionally, and for self-dual $\mathrm{GL}_3$ forms we obtain the same logarithmic exponent unconditionally. We also establish results under weaker bounds towards the Generalised Ramanujan--Petersson Conjecture together with the Generalised Lindel\"of Hypothesis, and obtain lower bounds for the number of sign changes and for the number of Hecke eigenvalues of each sign in long intervals.
item.dc:creator: Jesse J\"a\"asaari

item.title: On integers whose friable component is large
item.description: arXiv:2609.37507v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We estimate the number of integers up to $x$ whose $y$-friable component exceeds $z$. Uniformly for $\max\{2,\log z\}\leqslant y\leqslant z\leqslant x/2$, we determine the logarithm of this counting function up to an error $O(\log z/\log y)$. This sharpens an estimate arising from a problem in Ford's sieve methods lecture notes. The proof combines classical friable-number estimates with an elementary argument for the lower bound.
item.dc:creator: G\'erald Tenenbaum, Xiangyu Wang

item.title: A Short Proof of a Theorem of Pan and Zhang
item.description: arXiv:2609.37508v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pan and Zhang proved that a positive proportion of positive integers can be represented in the form $a^2+b^2+2^{c^2}$, where $(a,b,c)$ are nonnegative integers. In this note, we give a short proof of their result. The proof uses Romanoff's method and an elementary divisor argument to control the relevant second moment.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: A proof of Hirose's duality conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2609.40213v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hirose formulated a duality conjecture for a $q$-discretization of iterated integrals on the four-punctured projective line, incorporating word-dependent $q$-shifts of the parameters. In this paper, we prove this conjecture using a symmetric terminating ${}_{4}\phi_{3}$ connector.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichiro Seki

item.title: New bounds for the integer Chebyshev constant of [0,1]
item.description: arXiv:2610.00386v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The integer Chebyshev constant of [0,1] has been bracketed by 0.4213 <= t_Z([0,1]) <= 0.422685 since the work of Pritsker (2005) and of Flammang (2014). We prove 0.4222286000 <= t_Z([0,1]) <= 0.4226846976, narrowing the interval from 1.39e-3 to 4.56e-4. Both bounds are established by explicit certificates. The upper bound is carried by an integer polynomial with 92 factors and explicit integer exponents; the lower bound by a discrete measure on 947 cells together with a library of 206 irreducible polynomials, through an inequality in which the terms paying for divisibility are made explicit. Two self-contained scripts, included as ancillary files, re-derive both bounds from the certificates alone.
item.dc:creator: David Niedbala Giraudin

item.title: Indefinite theta vectors and generalized Nahm sums of arbitrary rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.00967v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct indefinite theta representations for a family of signed generalized Nahm sums of arbitrary rank \(r\geq2\). After explicit normalization and boundary correction, one signed branch gives the even components of a \((2r-1)\)-component holomorphic theta vector associated with a lattice of signature \((1,1)\). Euler-type multiple sums provide the odd components, yielding formulas uniform in both the rank and the component index. Using Zwegers' theory, we determine the weight-one modular transformation laws of the real-analytic completion, with an explicit finite sine matrix for the \(S\)-transformation. We decompose the nonholomorphic correction into a finite sum of products of unary theta functions and one-dimensional error-function series, and compute the antiholomorphic derivative of the completion. Together with the completed transformation laws, these formulas give the inhomogeneous transformation law of the holomorphic vector. We also evaluate a linear combination of two signed branches as a difference of Jacobi product quotients. This identity and further evaluations for two families of symmetrizable matrices and their duals, combined with known results, give multiple-sum representations for every component of four associated product vectors. These representations are finite combinations of generalized Nahm sums with the prescribed matrices and symmetrizers; in the dual families, half-period translates are absorbed into signs and constant phase factors.
item.dc:creator: Dandan Chen, Siyu Yin

item.title: Cohomology of Linearly Constrained Kloosterman Families: Newton Polytopes, Weights, and Boundary Monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2610.03081v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\psi$ a nontrivial additive character of $\mathbb F_p$, $\psi_q=\psi\circ\mathrm{Tr}_{\mathbb F_q/\mathbb F_p}$ and $\lambda\in\mathbb F_p^\times$. For $h\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ let $\Sigma_n(h)$ be the sum of $\psi_q(u_1^{-1}+\cdots+u_n^{-1})$ over $u\in(\mathbb F_q^\times)^n$ with $h_1u_1+\cdots+h_nu_n=-\lambda$, an additively twisted average of products of Kloosterman sums. For every $n\ge2$, the cohomology computing $\Sigma_n(h)$ is concentrated in one degree and has dimension $2^n-1$. It has $r(n)=2^n-\binom n{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$ eigenvalues of weight $n-1$, and its other eigenvalues are the integers $q^{k-1}$, $1\le k\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$, with ballot numbers as multiplicities. The part of top weight forms a lisse sheaf $\mathcal W_n$ of rank $r(n)$ on the torus $\mathbb G_m^n$. We determine its local monodromy at the coordinate boundary and its determinant: $\det\mathcal W_n$ is the Artin--Schreier sheaf of the sum $-2^{n-1}\lambda^{-1}(h_1+\cdots+h_n)$ of the critical values of the phase, twisted by $p^{(n+1)r(n)/2}$. The geometric monodromy group of $\mathcal W_n$, and the arithmetic one after normalization to weight $0$, are equal to $\{g\in\mathrm{GL}_{r(n)}:\det(g)^p=1\}$. Consequently the normalized sums become equidistributed like traces of Haar-random elements of $\{g\in\mathrm U(r(n)):\det(g)^p=1\}$. The proofs use Laumon's Fourier transform, middle convolution, the Cayley cubic surface and Larsen's alternative, but no classification of finite groups.
item.dc:creator: Hamed Ebadi

item.title: Prescribed Ideal Classes in Ennola Cubic Fields and Rational Points on Associated Elliptic Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.04254v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every prime $\ell\geq5$ and integer $n\geq2$, we construct an Ennola cubic field with a specified prime ideal above $\ell$ whose class has exact order $2^n$. For parameters satisfying two square conditions and explicit congruences, the same squareclass obstructions give four independent rational points on the associated elliptic curves. A Pell equation describes all such parameters. A genus-one base change gives five independent sections that generate a subgroup saturated at two. It also yields infinitely many elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$, pairwise nonisomorphic over $\overline{\mathbb Q}$, with rank at least five.
item.dc:creator: Junyu Lu

item.title: An Algebraic Proof of the Non-Modularity of Solutions to the Canonical Modular Differential Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.05668v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we provide an algebraic proof of the condition for the existence of modular form solutions to the Kaneko-Zagier differential equation of weight $k$. Unlike previous representation-theoretic approaches relying on $SL_2(\mathbb{Z})$, our method employs the connection matrices of the principal congruence subgroup $\Gamma(N)$. By deriving a condition for simultaneous triangularizability from the commutators of the representation matrices and applying Galois theory, we prove that the associated two-dimensional representation of $\Gamma(N)$ is irreducible when the denominator $m$ of the fraction $(k+1)/6 = n/m$ satisfies $m=1$ or $m \ge 7$. Consequently, we identify the weights that admit no modular form solutions and obtain a complete classification of the dimensions of the spaces of such solutions.
item.dc:creator: Yuichi Sakai, Hiroyuki Tsutsumi

item.title: A Bogomolov property for moduli spaces of polynomials over abelian extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.06382v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $d\geq2$ be an integer, and let $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ be the moduli space of degree-$d$ polynomials. For every number field $K$, we prove that there exists $\epsilon_{K,d}>0$ such that \[ \left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)<\epsilon_{K,d}\right\rbrace=\left\lbrace\alpha\in\operatorname{MPoly}^d(K^{\mathrm{ab}})\colon h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\alpha)=0\right\rbrace \] is finite, where $h_{\mathrm{crit}}$ is the critical height.
