In particular, only finitely many $K^{\mathrm{ab}}$-rational points of $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$ are postcritically finite. The proof combines the correspondence method of Ji--Song--Xie with local ramification estimates and the uniform finiteness of intertwined classes in $\operatorname{MPoly}^d$. We also prove an analogous finiteness theorem for non-preperiodic marked points in non-isotrivial one-parameter polynomial families.
item.dc:creator: Geng-Rui Zhang

item.title: The optimal van der Corput property for squares
item.description: arXiv:2610.07765v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative form of the van der Corput property for squares. For all sufficiently large $N$, we construct a real trigonometric polynomial $P(\theta)=a_0+\sum_{1\le n\le\sqrt N}a_n\cos(2\pi n^2\theta)$ satisfying \begin{equation}\tag{1}\label{eq:abstract-vdc} P(\theta)\ge0\quad(\theta\in\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}),\qquad P(0)=1, \end{equation} with \[0\le a_0\le\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] where $c>0$ is an absolute constant. As a consequence, if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}\cap[1,N]$ has no nonzero square difference, then \[|A|\le N\exp(-c\sqrt{\log N\log\log N}),\] improving upon a recent result of Green and Sawhney. Our construction builds on previous work of Slijep\v{c}evi\'c, Slijep\v{c}evi\'c--Nin\v{c}evi\'c, and Fan--Lott, and the proof of the upper bound is elementary and self-contained. We also show that every real trigonometric polynomial of the above form satisfying \eqref{eq:abstract-vdc} has \[a_0\ge\exp(-C\sqrt{\log N\log\log N})\] for an absolute constant $C>0$. Thus the van der Corput property cannot be used to obtain a power-saving bound for the Furstenberg--S\'ark\"ozy theorem.
item.dc:creator: Steve Fan, Andrew Lott

item.title: Maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding random points and lacunary dilates
item.description: arXiv:2610.09790v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive real lacunary sequence and any probability measure $\mu$ with polynomial Fourier decay, we determine, for $\mu$-almost every $x$, the asymptotic maximal volume of convex bodies avoiding the first $N$ dilates of $x$ modulo $\mathbb Z^d$. Among homothets of a fixed convex body, the maximal volume is asymptotic to $(\log N)/N$. When all convex bodies in the unit cube are allowed, it is asymptotic to $d(\log N)/N$. For independent uniform points in a fixed convex body $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$, the maximal volume of an empty convex body is asymptotic to $d\operatorname{vol}(\Omega)(\log N)/N$ almost surely. We also show, by constructing a one-dimensional counterexample, that lacunarity cannot be replaced by sparsity on sublacunary scales.
item.dc:creator: Yuval Peres, Bohan Yang

item.title: Logarithmic moments of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction and odd zeta values
item.description: arXiv:2610.10578v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the two cusp expansions of the Rogers-Ramanujan continued fraction control its ordinary and logarithmic Mellin moments. Ramanujan's factorizations express the logarithmic transform as a combination of products of zeta and quadratic Dirichlet $L$-functions. Its adjacent integer and half-integer values give an invertible change of coordinates for the corresponding odd special values. We prove that every reciprocal-cusp coefficient is a quadratic irrational algebraic integer, with an explicit minimal polynomial, and that every logarithmic coefficient is quadratic irrational. These facts determine the exact poles of three normalized-moment generating functions. The logarithmic one has an absolutely convergent partial fraction expansion with a pole at every positive square. For the ordinary moments, a two-cusp incomplete-gamma expansion gives meromorphic continuation at every positive splitting point. A general Mellin lemma yields the corresponding nonholonomicity statements. We also establish reflection identities, vertical strip decay and an explicit truncation estimate.
item.dc:creator: K. Srinivasa Raghava

item.title: Long intervals of consecutive composite values of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.10762v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $f\in\mathbb Q[t]$ be an irreducible polynomial of positive degree with positive leading coefficient, taking integer values at every integer. We prove that there is a constant $c_f>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large real $X$, the interval $(X/2,X]$ contains at least $c_f\log X\log\log X$ consecutive integers $n$ for which all values $f(n)$ are composite. The exponent of $\log\log X$ is independent of the degree of $f$. This improves the previous result of Ford and Gabdullin by replacing their small fixed power of $\log\log X$ with the full factor $\log\log X$. In particular, the result applies to $f(t)=t^2+1$.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Radomskii

item.title: A combinatorial proof of the quadratic Gauss sum
item.description: arXiv:2610.11075v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide an elementary approach to computing the quadratic Gauss sum, emphasizing the method employed to compute the sum corresponding to multiples of 4. The proof method employed does not rely on the law of quadratic reciprocity, but only on exploiting symmetries among the sum's components, together with a recursive approach.
item.dc:creator: Adan Medrano Martin del Campo

item.title: Improved zero-free half-planes for the quasi-Riemann hypothesis
item.dc:creator: Baiying Liu

item.title: On the Quantitative Bounds of Nonlinear Roth Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.13204v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that any subset $A \subseteq \{1, \dots, N\}$ lacking non-trivial polynomial progressions $(x, x + y, x + y^2)$ satisfies $\lvert A \rvert \le CN \exp\bigl(-c(\log \log N)^\beta\bigr)$ for effective absolute constants $C, c, \beta > 0$. The argument develops a density increment framework localized to anisotropic quadratic Bohr sets. To handle mixed linear and quadratic frequencies, we establish a multilinear transference principle coupled with a relative quadratic inverse theorem based on Balog--Szemer{\'e}di--Gowers additive energy rigidity. Boundary stability across increments is maintained via semi-algebraic model regularization using cylindrical algebraic decomposition and Cauchy--Crofton estimates, while dimension growth is controlled by dissociated basis reduction and multidimensional Erd{\H{o}}s--Tur{\'a}n--Koksma equidistribution.
item.dc:creator: Yunfan Zhao

item.title: Multiple Lattice Packings and Coverings of the Plane with Triangles
item.description: arXiv:1412.5096v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a convex disk $K$ and a positive integer $j$, let $\delta_L^j(K)$ and $\vartheta_L^j(K)$ denote the $j$-fold lattice packing density and the $j$-fold lattice covering density of $K$, respectively. I will prove that for every triangle $T$ we have that $\delta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j^2}{2j+1}$ and $\vartheta_L^j(T)=\frac{2j+1}{2}$. Furthermore, I also obtain that the numbers of lattices which attain these densities both are $(2j+1)\prod_{p|2j+1}(1-\frac{2}{p})$, where the product is over the distinct prime numbers dividing $2j+1$.
item.dc:creator: Kirati Sriamorn

item.title: Shifted symplectic structures on derived analytic moduli of $\ell$-adic local systems and Galois representations
item.description: arXiv:2205.02292v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a characterisation of non-Archimedean derived analytic geometry based on dg enhancements of dagger algebras. This allows us to formulate derived analytic moduli functors for many types of pro-\'etale sheaves, and to construct shifted symplectic structures on them by transgression using arithmetic duality theorems. In order to handle duality functors involving Tate twists, we introduce weighted shifted symplectic structures on formal weighted moduli stacks, with the usual moduli stacks given by taking $\mathbb{G}_m$-invariants. In particular, this establishes the existence of shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic constructible complexes on smooth varieties via Poincar\'e duality, and on derived moduli stacks of $\ell$-adic Galois representations via Tate and Poitou--Tate duality; the latter proves a conjecture of Minhyong Kim. Unweighted shifted symplectic and Lagrangian structures are also established for $\ell$-adic Galois representations of cyclotomic fields $K(\mu_{\ell^{\infty}})$, subject to additional constraints related to Iwasawa theory; these derived moduli stacks yield a non-abelian analogue of Selmer complexes, with $0$-shifted symplectic structures related to generalised Cassels--Tate pairings.
item.dc:creator: J. P. Pridham

item.title: The Hurwitz tree obstruction for the refined local lifting problem
item.description: arXiv:2405.01845v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the differential Hurwitz tree obstruction for the cyclic $p$-power refined local lifting problem always vanishes. Given a cyclic extension of degree $p^n$ in characteristic $p$ and a lift of its degree-$p^{n-1}$ subextension, we construct a compatible differential Hurwitz tree extending the tree of that lift. Realizing the resulting tree by a cover remains a separate problem.
item.dc:creator: Huy Dang

item.title: Monochromatic non-commuting products
item.description: arXiv:2405.03772v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that a finite coloring of an amenable group contains `many' monochromatic sets of the form $\{x,y,xy,yx\},$ and natural extensions with more variables. This gives the first combinatorial proof and extensions of Bergelson and McCutcheon's non-commutative Schur theorem. Our main new tool is the introduction of what we call `quasirandom colorings,' a condition that is automatically satisfied by colorings of quasirandom groups, and a reduction to this case.
item.dc:creator: Matt Bowen

item.title: Asymptotics of rational representations for algebraic groups
item.description: arXiv:2405.17360v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the cohomology of subgroups $\Gamma$ of an algebraic group $G$ with coefficients in the various irreducible rational representations of $G$ and raise a conjecture about it. Namely, we expect that the dimensions of these cohomology groups approximate the L2-analogues of Betti numbers of $\Gamma$ with a controlled error term. We provide positive answers when $G$ is a product of copies of $SL_2$.
item.dc:creator: Lander Guerrero S\'anchez, Henrique Souza

item.title: An algebraic proof of Hrushovski's theorem
item.description: arXiv:2409.08370v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In his paper on the Mordell-Lang conjecture, Hrushovski employed techniques from model theory to prove the function field version of the conjecture. In doing so he was able to answer a related question of Voloch, which we refer to henceforth as Hrushovski's theorem. In this paper we shall give an alternative proof of said theorem in the characteristic $p$ setting, but using purely algebro-geometric ideas.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Wisson

item.title: The Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for commutative algebraic groups with unipotent rank 1
item.description: arXiv:2502.10379v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $k$ be algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, let $G$ be a commutative algebraic group over $k$ such that the linear part of $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{G}_a$, and let $X$ be a closed subvariety of $G$. We show that the Kawamata locus of $X$ is equal to a Lang-like exceptional locus of $X$, and furthermore, we identify a condition on $X$ that implies that these loci are proper subschemes of $X$. Using this, we prove the strong form of the Green--Griffiths--Lang--Vojta conjecture for closed subvarieties of $\mathbb{G}_a \times A$ where $A$ is an abelian variety.
item.dc:creator: Jackson S. Morrow, Paul Vojta

item.title: The Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent
item.description: arXiv:2503.20570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the Shafarevich conjecture for varieties with globally generated cotangent bundle, subject to mild numerical conditions.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Kr\"amer, Marco Maculan

item.title: Maps between circle bundles: Fiber-preserving, Finiteness and Realization of mapping degree sets
item.description: arXiv:2505.16285v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $E_i$ be an oriented circle bundle over a closed oriented $n$-manifold $M_i$ with $i=1,2$ and assume that $M_2$ is aspherical. We prove the following geometric realization result, which extends the classical result for maps between circle bundles over surfaces to all dimensions $\geq 2$. Let $f\colon E_1\to E_2$ be a map. If the induced homomorphism $f_*$ on $\pi_1$ sends the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_1)$ to the fiber subgroup of $\pi_1(E_2)$, then there is a fiber-preserving map in the homotopy class of $f$. Using the above result and a computation of the mapping degree set of fiber-preserving maps between $E_1$ and $E_2$, we obtain the following results on the finiteness and the realization problems of mapping degree sets. ($\mathcal F$) The mapping degree set $D(E_1, E_2)$ is finite if $M_2$ is hyperbolic and the Euler class of $E_2$ is not torsion. ($\mathcal R$) For any finite set $A$ of integers containing $0$ and any $n>2$, $A$ is the mapping degree set $D(M,N)$ for some closed oriented $n$-manifolds $M$ and $N$. Item ($\mathcal F$) extends the previously known $3$-dimensional case to all dimensions $\geq 3$. Item ($\mathcal R$) gives a complete answer to the realization problem on finite sets of integers (containing 0) in all dimensions, including in particular the previously unknown cases in dimensions $ 4$ and $5$.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis, Hongbin Sun, Ye Tian, Shicheng Wang, Zhongzi Wang

item.title: Recurrence for pretentious systems along generalized Pythagorean triples
item.description: arXiv:2508.09778v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish multiple recurrence results for pretentious measure-preserving multiplicative actions along generalized Pythagorean triples, that is, solutions to the equation $ax^2 + b y^2 = c z^2$. This confirms the ergodic-theoretic form of the generalized Pythagorean partition regularity conjecture in this critical case of structured measure-preserving actions. As a consequence of our main theorem, any finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by the level sets of finitely many pretentious completely multiplicative functions, must contain a monochromatic generalized Pythagorean triple.
item.dc:creator: Nikos Frantzikinakis, Andreas Mountakis

item.title: Une conjecture $C_{\rm st}$ pour la cohomologie \`a support compact
item.description: arXiv:2511.14675v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbf{B}$ be the ring of analytic functions on the Fargues-Fontaine curve $Y_{\rm FF}$. We shaw that, by adding sufficiently iterated periods, one can kill its Galois cohomology in degrees $\geq 1$. For $\mathbf{B}_{\rm dR}^+$, the corresponding result is obtained by adjoining just $\log t$ and is folklore. This allows to formulate $C_{\rm dR}$ and $C_{\rm st}$ conjectures for the compactly supported cohomology of $p$-adic analytic varieties.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Colmez, Sally Gilles, Wies{\l}awa Nizio{\l}

item.title: Conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices
item.description: arXiv:2602.15748v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to the theory of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer $n\times n$ matrices and related commutative semigroups. Such a matrix is $GL_n({\mathbb Q})$-conjugate to the companion matrix of its characteristic polynomial. But the set of $GL_n({\mathbb Z})$-conjugacy classes of regular integer matrices with a fixed characteristic polynomial $f$ is usually nontrivial (finite if $f$ has simple roots, infinite if $f$ has multiple roots). It is in 1:1-correspondence to a subsemigroup of a certain quotient semigroup of the commutative semigroup of full lattices in the algebra ${\mathbb Q}[t]/(f)$. In its first part, the paper gives a survey on old and new results on full lattices and orders in a finite dimensional commutative ${\mathbb Q}$-algebra with unit element and on induced semigroups. In its longer second part, the paper applies this theory to many examples, essentially all cases with $n=2$, many cases with $n=3$ and two cases with arbitrary $n$, the case with $n$ different integer eigenvalues and the case of a single $n\times n$ Jordan block.
item.dc:creator: Claus Hertling, Khadija Larabi

item.title: Galois Orbit Bounds for Surface Degenerations
item.description: arXiv:2603.02606v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given a smooth proper family $g : X \to S$ of surfaces over a number field $K \subset \mathbb{C}$, with $S$ an irreducible curve and $\eta \in S$ its generic point, we consider the general problem of constraining the locus $\textrm{NL}(S)$ in $S(\overline{K})$ of points $s$ where the Picard rank of $X_{s}$ is larger than the generic Picard rank. Assuming that the local system $\mathbb{V} = R^{2} g_{*} \mathbb{Z}$ admits a non-trivial monodromy logarithm $N$ at infinity, we give a general condition under which certain points of $\textrm{NL}(S)$ of unexpectedly large Picard rank satisfy a ``Galois-orbit'' height bound. This leads to the following result of Zilber-Pink type: Let $g : X \to S$ be a one-parameter family of polarized K3 surfaces admitting a non-trivial limit mixed Hodge structure and such that $S(\mathbb{C})$ contains a Hodge-generic point. Then the locus in $S(\mathbb{C})$ where the Picard rank jumps by $3$ or more is finite. Our arguments include a new technique for ``spreading out'' formal geometry, a study of the rigid geometry of equicharacteristic zero semistable surface degenerations, and use the model-free Hyodo-Kato theory of Colmez-Nizio\l.
item.dc:creator: David Urbanik

item.title: A topological interpretation of numbers
item.description: arXiv:2607.26926v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We survey recent advancements on the realisation problem for mapping degree sets. In particular, we explain that any finite set containing zero is the mapping degree set between some $n$-manifolds, for each $n\geq3$. Our building factors for the construction of the realising manifolds will be aspherical manifolds. Thus, along the way, we review a couple of open questions related to maps of non-zero degree for aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Christoforos Neofytidis

item.title: The Five Distance Theorem For An Arbitrary Norm
item.description: arXiv:2608.12405v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The three gap theorem states that the points of the Kronecker sequence $\alpha,2\alpha,\ldots,N\alpha$, considered modulo one, divide the circle into intervals of at most three distinct lengths. In a two-dimensional nearest-neighbour analogue, Haynes and Marklof proved that the Kronecker sequence modulo an arbitrary unimodular lattice determines at most five distinct nearest-neighbour distances in the Euclidean norm, and that this bound is sharp. Dettmann subsequently constructed examples attaining five distinct distances for every $\ell_p$-norm, $1\leq p\leq\infty$. We prove the corresponding upper bound for every norm on $\mathbb R^2$: for every full-rank lattice $L$, every $\alpha\in\mathbb R^2$, and every $N\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct nearest-neighbour distances is at most five. For every norm, this bound is attained for some $L$ and $\alpha$. For strictly convex norms, the proof extends the lattice-theoretic argument of Haynes and Marklof by replacing the Euclidean angular estimates with a cone lemma based on a proper Brass angular measure. The result for arbitrary norms is then obtained by a strictly convex perturbation and a limiting argument.
item.dc:creator: Nikita A. Mironov, Oleg R. Musin

item.title: On Frobenius rigidity for motivic cohomology
item.description: arXiv:2608.27834v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how motivic and \'etale motivic cohomology of a smooth and proper variety changes under extensions of algebraically closed base fields $k$. With finite coefficients, motivic cohomology is independent of $k$, and \'etale motivic cohomology is independent of $k$ away from the characteristic, but depends on $k$ at the characteristic. We then consider the fiber of $F-1$ for $F$ the Frobenius, on motivic cohomology and \'etale motivic cohomology for varieties defined over finite fields. We show that this fiber is independent of $k$ with finite coefficients. In addition, we give some results and examples with integral coefficients.

item.title: Affine Symmetries of Polynomial Roots with Multiplicities and Applications to Constacyclic Codes
item.description: arXiv:2609.26414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $f(X)$ be a polynomial over a finite field, and let its defining function record the multiplicities of its roots. In this paper, we introduce the affine stabilizer group and the affine stabilizer group scheme of the defining function of $f(X)$. These objects characterize the affine symmetries of the roots of $f(X)$ together with their multiplicities. We establish structural descriptions of these affine stabilizers and relate them to the coefficient structure of $f(X)$. In particular, the affine stabilizer group determines quotient structures of the defining function, which yield canonical descriptions of the corresponding semi-invariant polynomial spaces. The resulting coefficient constraints provide explicit restrictions on the possible supports of polynomials with prescribed affine symmetries. The affine stabilizer group scheme further captures infinitesimal symmetries arising from multiple roots and gives refined coefficient constraints beyond those obtained from ordinary affine transformations. We apply this framework to generator polynomials of constacyclic codes over finite fields. The affine stabilizer structure of a generator polynomial induces subcodes defined by semi-invariant conditions and provides constraints on their dimensions and Hamming distances. In the special case of multiplicative symmetries, the construction specializes to the support-primitive decomposition of constacyclic codes.

item.title: The Bias Conjecture for One-Parameter, Non-Isotrivial Elliptic Curve Families
item.description: arXiv:2609.38664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate Miller's bias conjecture for general one-parameter families of elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$ with non-constant $j$-invariants. Utilizing methods developed by Michel, we view the second moment as the sum of distinct cohomological components: a main $p^2$ term, a $p^{3/2}$ term arising from the first cohomology over the projective line, and terms of order $p$ or lower corresponding to singular fibers. By assuming the generalized Sato-Tate conjecture, we employ representation and motive theory to demonstrate that the coefficient of the $p^{3/2}$ term averages to zero in the limit. We then independently analyze the lower-order contributions without assuming Sato-Tate. By applying the Chebotarev density theorem and analyzing Galois representations, we show that the contributions to the order $p$ term from additive singular fibers also average to zero. Consequently, the only remaining average contribution to the $p$ term is $-B_pp$, where $B_p$ denotes the number of ``bad'' points where the discriminant vanishes. Because $B_p$ averages to a strictly positive value, the overall coefficient of the $p$ term averages to a strictly negative value in the limit, thereby establishing the bias conjecture for these families.

item.title: Ekedahl's Equivalence Explained
item.description: arXiv:2609.39293v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ekedahl's theory relates diagonal complexes to \(F\)-gauges, but turning this equivalence into explicit calculations requires careful control of its constructions. These notes explain the equivalence and clarify the generators-and-relations definition of \(\rmt\). At each finite level, we construct bounded projective resolutions of bounded coherent gauge complexes by finite sums of the standard generators. Morita equivalence expresses \(\rmt\) as a tensor product functor. Comparing the constructions across levels yields an exact fully faithful embedding of the diagonal heart into \(\Ch(R)\). Finally, we compute three distinct domino types arising from abelian threefolds that are all supergeneral.

item.title: Mock Modularity, Resurgence, and Dual False Theta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.00516v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The $\hat{Z}$ invariant of a three-manifold $M_{3}$, a half-index of the $3d$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ theory $T[M_{3}]$, is well understood for negative-definite plumbed three-manifolds. For orientation-reversed manifolds, however, the known formulas fail to produce $q$-series, and making sense of the operation $q \rightarrow q^{-1}$ remains a central open problem. Seifert manifolds, whose $\hat{Z}$ invariants are built from false theta functions, offer a natural testing ground. We study ``dual false theta functions'', the objects that should replace false theta functions under orientation reversal. Two characterizations of these duals exist in the literature: a modular one, based on mock modularity with a prescribed shadow, and a resurgent one, based on Borel--Mordell integrals and transseries. We prove that the two characterizations are equivalent. We construct a new family of dual false theta functions for values of positive integer $p$ satisfying a Pell-equation condition. Its members are built from Zwegers' indefinite theta functions, have integer coefficients, and have effective central charge $c_{\text{eff}} \leq 1$. We also show that the mock theta functions of Li and Schwagenscheidt satisfy these characterizations and arise from a natural regularization of the divergent product $\eta^{3}(\tau)\psi_{p, a}(- \tau)$.

item.title: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12071v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero. More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.
